id: static-top-k expert allocation inefficiency
name: static-top-k expert allocation inefficiency
description: The paper addresses the problem of fixed compute overhead in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models due to rigid top-*k* expert selection per token, wasting resources on irrelevant experts even when fewer are sufficient.

id: misaligned category-granularity routing
name: misaligned category-granularity routing
description: The problem is that learned routers in mixture-of-experts fail to outperform dense baselines when the training signal’s category granularity does not align with the target modular specialization, even at matched parameter budgets.

id: inefficient MoE speculative decoding expert activation
name: inefficient MoE speculative decoding expert activation
description: The problem is that speculative decoding for MoE models wastes computational resources by activating all possible experts for every draft token in the verification tree, even when only a subset of those tokens will be accepted, leading to unnecessary expert union expansion and traffic overhead.

id: uncertainty-driven expert routing misclassification
name: uncertainty-driven expert routing misclassification
description: The paper addresses how dynamic routing in Mixture-of-LoRA-Experts (MoLE) fails to distinguish between ambiguous inputs that could benefit from additional expert evidence and those that remain unresolved despite querying all experts, leading to incorrect abstention or over-reliance on uncertainty as a routing signal.

id: irreducible per-round loss from representation aliasing
name: irreducible per-round loss from representation aliasing
description: The paper addresses the problem of agents failing to detect and recover from compressed history representations that merge distinct action-optimal trajectories, causing unavoidable task loss that cannot be measured or mitigated by rules derived from the representation alone.

gap_flag.short_label: Irreducible per-round loss from representation aliasing
gap_flag.falsifiability_note: this is a real gap if no existing published theory already covers this exact self-certification framing under a comparable cost model. It would be undermined by prior, uncited work establishing an equivalent bound.

id: unified geospatial multimodal retrieval gap
name: unified geospatial multimodal retrieval gap
description: The lack of a shared embedding space capable of jointly modeling heterogeneous geospatial data (e.g., street-view imagery, remote sensing, text, regions, temporal cues) for diverse urban tasks like spatial reasoning, fine-grained semantics, and change detection.

id: attention misalignment with typographic salience cues
name: attention misalignment with typographic salience cues
description: The paper identifies that large pretrained models fail to align their internal attention mechanisms with human-like salience cues (e.g., uppercase letters) in text, causing unintended attention shifts that do not consistently improve downstream performance.

id: real-time kinematic incident detection under privacy constraints
name: real-time kinematic incident detection under privacy constraints
description: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately recognizing classroom incidents from CCTV-style video while preserving privacy and computational efficiency, where existing methods fail due to limited benchmarks, high resource demands, and poor generalization to real-world motion dynamics.

id: modality interaction asymmetry in unified pretraining
name: modality interaction asymmetry in unified pretraining
description: The abstract addresses how and why language, vision, and visual generation modalities exhibit uneven, context-dependent knowledge transfer during joint pretraining, including delayed integration pitfalls like 'vision laziness' and the role of data complexity in shaping synergy or competition.

id: ambiguous cross-modal correspondence alignment
name: ambiguous cross-modal correspondence alignment
description: The paper addresses the challenge of establishing reliable one-to-one mappings between heterogeneous representations (charts, tables, and code) where supervision is scarce, relationships are inherently multi-mapped, and existing methods lack a generalizable consistency signal for cross-representation learning.

id: frame-level temporal cues underutilization in V2A
name: frame-level temporal cues underutilization in V2A
description: Existing video-to-audio generation methods fail to effectively exploit raw temporal differences between consecutive frames as a standalone visual representation, instead relying on costly auxiliary networks or strong inductive biases.

id: cross-task unlearning interference in continual MLLMs
name: cross-task unlearning interference in continual MLLMs
description: The paper addresses how repeated one-shot unlearning requests in continual multimodal large language models cause harmful cross-task interference—where prior unlearning adapters degrade new unlearning effectiveness and retained knowledge—while also missing opportunities for positive transfer between tasks.

id: symbolic music agent comprehension gaps
name: symbolic music agent comprehension gaps
description: The abstract addresses how music co-creation agents fail to robustly extract hierarchical musical structure (e.g., phrase boundaries, harmonic content) from unlabeled MIDI data without explicit music-theory supervision, limiting their ability to generate contextually coherent suggestions.

id: adversarial robustness in multi-model perception fusion
name: adversarial robustness in multi-model perception fusion
description: The problem is that combining imperfect pre-trained ViT-based detectors via simple combiners (e.g., majority voting) fails catastrophically under coordinated adversarial attacks or distributional shifts, lacking adaptive error-detection without domain-specific cues.

id: background-set dependency in music distortion detection
name: background-set dependency in music distortion detection
description: The inability of existing reference-free music quality metrics to generalize without relying on precomputed statistics from a fixed set of clean audio samples, limiting their applicability to unseen or evolving audio distributions.

id: multimodal intent recognition's conflict-ignorance bias
name: multimodal intent recognition's conflict-ignorance bias
description: The abstract targets the failure of existing multimodal intent recognition systems to explicitly model and leverage cross-modal disagreements (e.g., sarcasm cues) while suppressing only incidental noise, instead of either forcing alignment or discarding all inconsistencies as uncertainty.

id: CLIPScore distribution overlap in backdoor detection
name: CLIPScore distribution overlap in backdoor detection
description: The inability to reliably distinguish poisoned from benign multimodal pairs due to overlapping CLIPScore distributions in contrastive learning datasets like CC3M, undermining fixed-threshold backdoor detection methods.

id: cross-sensor, multi-resolution road segmentation generalization
name: cross-sensor, multi-resolution road segmentation generalization
description: The inability of existing road network segmentation models to maintain consistent, connected predictions across varying satellite sensors, resolutions (0.3–1.0 m), and geographic regions due to domain shifts and limited generalization.

id: open-vocabulary tactile recognition from resistive pressure arrays
name: open-vocabulary tactile recognition from resistive pressure arrays
description: The paper addresses the challenge of recognizing arbitrary objects from low-cost resistive pressure sensor data without relying on optical tactile sensors or pre-defined class labels, where prior methods fail due to limited sensor diversity and lack of scalable open-vocabulary generalization.

id: inverted-steering vectors in concept alignment
name: inverted-steering vectors in concept alignment
description: The paper addresses the counterintuitive failure where highly discriminative steering vectors (intended to promote a concept) instead suppress it during representation alignment, breaking the linear discriminability assumption in concept steering for large language models.

id: adaptive multimodal fusion granularity
name: adaptive multimodal fusion granularity
description: Determining the optimal cross-modal integration level in supervised learning is problematic because fixed fusion strategies either over-amplify noise or underutilize intermodal dependencies in heterogeneous data.

id: training-log covariate bias in stochastic model comparisons
name: training-log covariate bias in stochastic model comparisons
description: The abstract targets the problem of unreliable uncertainty estimates in stochastic model comparisons due to unaccounted-for training-log covariates, where blindly selecting noisy statistics from logs worsens precision in performance-difference estimation.

id: scalable long-range traffic trajectory hallucination
name: scalable long-range traffic trajectory hallucination
description: The paper addresses the challenge of generating statistically realistic, coherent, and hallucination-free long-range (extended field-of-view) traffic trajectories in automated driving simulations, where existing GAN-based methods fail to maintain object permanence and spatial consistency across larger, more complex scenes.

id: state-interval localization in object histories
name: state-interval localization in object histories
description: The problem of distinguishing and localizing temporally contiguous but visually ambiguous object states (e.g., empty/full, intact/cut) in long-term visual tracking histories when absolute similarity scores fail to disambiguate due to shared object identity.

id: multilingual visual QA answer format fragility
name: multilingual visual QA answer format fragility
description: The system struggles with maintaining strict, artifact-free, and concise answer formats in multilingual visual question answering (VQA) tasks where outputs must adhere to precise labels (MCQ) or clean, reasoning-free text (OpenQA) across dense, multimodal educational/scientific inputs.

id: cross-dataset novelty detection failure
name: cross-dataset novelty detection failure
description: Self-supervised predictive architectures like JEPA fail to reliably identify truly novel driving clips when evaluated across datasets due to domain-shift artifacts, conflating novelty with dataset separation.

id: role-based, power-structured perspective coordination
name: role-based, power-structured perspective coordination
description: The abstract targets the failure of current pluralistic alignment systems to model how values are socially organized by roles, power dynamics, and interactional fields—limiting their ability to accountably coordinate conflicting perspectives in agentic AI.

id: misleading explanations in dependent causal inputs
name: misleading explanations in dependent causal inputs
description: Existing neural network explanation methods fail to account for structured input dependencies, leading to incorrect or inflated actual-cause attributions in scenarios where features are causally related.

id: Lack of unified design principles for trustworthy AI integration
name: Lack of unified design principles for trustworthy AI integration
description: The absence of systematic, cross-cutting guidelines for combining machine learning with formal reasoning in AI systems—limiting their reliability, interpretability, and scalability across high-stakes and low-data domains.

id: causal analysis of unstructured outcomes
name: causal analysis of unstructured outcomes
description: The inability to compute meaningful average treatment effects when outcomes are high-dimensional (e.g., text, images) due to lack of a natural subtraction operation, requiring new causal queries like maximally contrasting features (MCF).

id: separating latent confounders from irreducible stochasticity in counterfactual MDPs
name: separating latent confounders from irreducible stochasticity in counterfactual MDPs
description: The paper targets the failure of existing counterfactual methods to distinguish between hidden global confounders (e.g., diabetes status) and irreducible environmental noise in stochastic MDPs, causing incorrect counterfactual attribution in sequential decision-making.

id: cross-cultural ethical acceptance gaps in care robots
name: cross-cultural ethical acceptance gaps in care robots
description: The paper examines how caregivers from diverse national contexts (US, Mexico, Chile) perceive and prioritize ethical trade-offs in care robots—balancing benefits like workload reduction against risks like job displacement and dependability—while revealing culturally nuanced variations in stakeholder concerns.

id: legal-technical misalignment in XAI compliance
name: legal-technical misalignment in XAI compliance
description: The gap between EU legal requirements for human-readable, purpose-specific explanations (e.g., GDPR Art. 15(1)(h), AI Act Art. 86) and the technical capabilities of current XAI systems to deliver them in practice.

id: AI authority delegation gaps in financial decisions
name: AI authority delegation gaps in financial decisions
description: The abstract identifies the problem of **how little real-world financial execution authority users delegate to AI** despite heavy reliance on AI for information retrieval and judgment shaping in real financial interactions.

id: few-shot tabular domain shift adaptation
name: few-shot tabular domain shift adaptation
description: The paper addresses the challenge of generating accurate target-domain tabular data when only a small number of sparse target records are available, while existing methods either overfit noisy target statistics or fail to adapt source-domain dependency structures that no longer apply.

id: hidden confounder identification in spatiotemporal interference
name: hidden confounder identification in spatiotemporal interference
description: The paper addresses the challenge of estimating causal effects when hidden confounders bias treatment-outcome relationships and spatial/temporal dependencies (interference) exist in real-world spatiotemporal data, where standard methods fail due to unobserved covariates.

id: deployment-aware quantization for closed-loop WAMs
name: deployment-aware quantization for closed-loop WAMs
description: The abstract addresses the challenge of applying post-training quantization to World Action Models (WAMs) where traditional methods fail due to mismatched calibration distributions between open-loop training and iterative, closed-loop deployment scenarios.

id: adaptive denoising step termination in diffusion policies
name: adaptive denoising step termination in diffusion policies
description: The abstract addresses the problem of inefficient fixed-step denoising in diffusion-based continuous control policies, where excessive iterations waste compute without meaningful performance gains, particularly in MuJoCo environments.

id: latent-dynamics defect accumulation in long-horizon diffusion world models
name: latent-dynamics defect accumulation in long-horizon diffusion world models
description: the inability of existing caching methods to detect and correct latent transition errors that compound over skipped steps in long-term latent evolution, particularly under phase- or condition-dependent drift in diffusion-based world models

id: multiplicative Gamma-noise image restoration
name: multiplicative Gamma-noise image restoration
description: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately restoring images degraded by **multiplicative Gamma noise and blur**, where existing deep equilibrium models either lack explicit, geometrically interpretable regularization or fail to converge efficiently under such noise conditions.

id: interpreting learned spatial filtering in CNNs
name: interpreting learned spatial filtering in CNNs
description: The abstract addresses the problem of *explaining how convolutional neural networks (e.g., DnCNN) implicitly perform spatially adaptive filtering* by mapping their learned dynamics to classical signal-processing concepts like bilateral filtering, without requiring differentiability.

id: dynamical redundancy in ESN reservoirs
name: dynamical redundancy in ESN reservoirs
description: The abstract addresses the problem of **unnecessary dynamic redundancy in Echo State Network reservoirs**, where randomly initialized neurons contribute little to meaningful state transitions during temporal prediction, undermining efficiency without being identified by static pruning criteria.

id: feature dispersion in multimodal tabular-image fusion
name: feature dispersion in multimodal tabular-image fusion
description: The abstract addresses how unstructured feature ordering in joint image-tabular learning causes redundant, scattered representations that degrade generalization, particularly in multimodal benchmarks where tabular and visual modalities are fused.

id: OOD robustness of tabular-to-image classifiers
name: OOD robustness of tabular-to-image classifiers
description: The paper examines how test-time augmentation fails or succeeds to maintain predictive accuracy when tabular data representations (via six encoding methods) shift beyond their training distribution (evaluated on HELOC and Voting datasets).

id: high-frequency, spatially inefficient adversarial perturbations for face-swap defense
name: high-frequency, spatially inefficient adversarial perturbations for face-swap defense
description: The abstract targets the problem of adversarial perturbations for deepfake defense being both spectrally wasteful (excessive high-frequency noise) and spatially inefficient (spread across non-identity-critical regions) in face-swap countermeasures.

id: multi-step ODE trajectory misalignment in flow-matching VLAs
name: multi-step ODE trajectory misalignment in flow-matching VLAs
description: The abstract targets the vulnerability of flow-matching vision-language-action models’ robustness claims, where adversarial attacks fail to exploit the *cumulative, multi-step denoising ODE trajectory* (not just initial perturbations) during test-time policy execution.

id: nonlinear full-wave permittivity reconstruction
name: nonlinear full-wave permittivity reconstruction
description: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately recovering unknown permittivity contrasts from electromagnetic scattering data in scenarios with strong multiple scattering, where classical methods and deep learning baselines fail to enforce nonlinear wave physics and produce artifacts.

id: out-of-distribution scaling mismatch in ptychography reconstructions
name: out-of-distribution scaling mismatch in ptychography reconstructions
description: The inability of ptychography neural networks to maintain consistent measurement scaling when deployed across varying experimental illumination conditions, degrading reconstruction accuracy in real-world, facility-specific deployments.

id: limited-neural-data generalization in motor BCIs
name: limited-neural-data generalization in motor BCIs
description: The paper addresses the challenge of poor cross-session, cross-subject, and cross-task motor trajectory decoding performance in brain-computer interfaces when neural data is scarce and heterogeneous, by leveraging pretrained behavioral representations to improve generalization under fixed neural recording constraints.

id: cross-sensor sedentary behavior classification drift
name: cross-sensor sedentary behavior classification drift
description: The paper addresses the degradation of posture-based sedentary behavior classification accuracy when transferring a hip-worn accelerometer model to wrist-worn data due to sensor placement differences, requiring domain-specific adaptation.

id: high-frequency EEG dynamical feature extraction for disorder classification
name: high-frequency EEG dynamical feature extraction for disorder classification
description: The paper addresses the challenge of reliably extracting and distinguishing consistent high-frequency dynamical patterns in EEG signals—specifically from neurologically relevant channels—to enable classification of brain disorders (e.g., alcohol dependence) from control groups.

id: minimal IMU-based GRF estimation for PD gait variability
name: minimal IMU-based GRF estimation for PD gait variability
description: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating ground reaction forces (GRFs) in Parkinson’s disease gait using a minimal, optimized set of IMUs, where high gait variability and existing multi-sensor approaches limit practicality and patient compliance.

id: frozen transformer input-embedding structural similarity detection
name: frozen transformer input-embedding structural similarity detection
description: The paper addresses the challenge of reliably distinguishing and comparing structural patterns in frozen transformer input-embedding spaces using deterministic, probe-based response signatures, where traditional task-based metrics fail to capture inherent embedding-level organization.

id: spectral imbalance in EEG foundation models
name: spectral imbalance in EEG foundation models
description: EEG foundation models systematically overemphasize low-frequency components due to $1/f^α$-like spectral structure and reconstruction objectives, degrading transferability across diverse downstream tasks.

id: uninterpretable MEG-to-speech retrieval feature attribution
name: uninterpretable MEG-to-speech retrieval feature attribution
description: The paper addresses the lack of clear understanding of which specific speech features (e.g., silence, intensity, vowels) and cortical sources drive speech reconstruction from MEG recordings, despite high retrieval accuracy.

id: realistic coding task environment reconstruction from historical changes
name: realistic coding task environment reconstruction from historical changes
description: The paper addresses the challenge of generating high-fidelity, executable coding tasks with reliable verification from real-world repository changes, ensuring tasks are grounded in authentic software states and development contexts while minimizing redundant setup and storage overhead.

id: cross-backend, long-horizon task execution failure
name: cross-backend, long-horizon task execution failure
description: The inability of LLM agents to consistently execute open-ended, multi-step, cross-environment tasks while preserving goals, managing context overflow, and ensuring deliverable correctness across different LLM backends.

id: scalable, verifiable long-horizon computer-agent training
name: scalable, verifiable long-horizon computer-agent training
description: the challenge of training agents to perform arbitrary, multi-step software tasks from raw visual input (screenshots) and sparse, delayed rewards across diverse, unstructured environments without task-specific APIs or structured data

id: delayed ordinal preference learning
name: delayed ordinal preference learning
description: The challenge of training video editing agents to optimize subjective, multi-step outcomes when feedback is only available after final rollout, not intermediate steps, and lacks consistent calibration across diverse tasks.

id: embodied-agent replanning latency tail risks
name: embodied-agent replanning latency tail risks
description: The paper addresses the critical failure mode where embodied agents’ replanning latency exhibits heavy-tailed distributions, causing real-time deadline misses despite high task success, particularly as accumulated textual context grows across replanning calls.

id: flat-skill-document retrieval inefficiency
name: flat-skill-document retrieval inefficiency
description: Retrieving skills from large, structured skill banks suffers when skills are treated as unstructured concatenated documents, failing to leverage field-specific relevance signals in multi-field skill representations.

id: unstable credit assignment in long-horizon trajectory learning
name: unstable credit assignment in long-horizon trajectory learning
description: The paper addresses how arbitrary, fixed, or retrospective segmentation methods fail to align with the true causal phases of agent-generated trajectories, causing misaligned credit assignment during training on long-horizon tasks.

id: persistent experience internalization in LLMs
name: persistent experience internalization in LLMs
description: The paper addresses how to convert transient interaction data from LLMs into lasting, updatable model capabilities without relying solely on either test-time extraction or training-time optimization alone.

id: cross-departmental operational siloing in replenishment planning
name: cross-departmental operational siloing in replenishment planning
description: The abstract targets the failure of fragmented, department-specific optimization in supply-chain replenishment—where assortment, sourcing, frequency, and routing decisions are treated independently despite their interdependent impact on system-wide efficiency and cost.

id: large-action-space regret minimization
name: large-action-space regret minimization
description: The paper targets the challenge of efficiently minimizing cumulative regret in contextual bandits when the action space is so vast that exploration becomes sparse, feedback is partial, and standard methods fail due to high variance, extrapolation bias, and optimization difficulties.

id: interference-aware peer-to-peer critic coordination
name: interference-aware peer-to-peer critic coordination
description: The paper addresses the challenge of enabling decentralized, low-communication coordination among cell-level controllers in **reuse-1 massive-MIMO OFDMA 6G RANs** to jointly optimize scheduling, power allocation, beamforming, and interference management without centralized training or actor federation, while preserving finite-time stability guarantees.

id: DSP bid-throttling under RTB over-distribution
name: DSP bid-throttling under RTB over-distribution
description: The abstract targets the inefficiency of blindly forwarding all real-time bidding (RTB) ad requests to demand-side platforms (DSPs), which causes DSPs to throttle bids due to compute/budget constraints, wasting limited bidding capacity and degrading auction outcomes.

id: simulator ambiguity decay in sequential control
name: simulator ambiguity decay in sequential control
description: The problem is that control policies trained in simulators with parameter uncertainty that diminishes over time (due to state-dependent inference) lose robustness to latent shifts in real systems where ambiguity must persist.

id: asymptotic engagement loss in heavy-tailed content ecosystems
name: asymptotic engagement loss in heavy-tailed content ecosystems
description: The paper identifies that symmetric two-sided isolation in large-scale content platforms causes persistent, non-vanishing engagement loss when the distribution of match quality follows heavy tails, even as the candidate pool grows exponentially.

id: real-time incentive allocation under non-Markovian user fatigue
name: real-time incentive allocation under non-Markovian user fatigue
description: The paper addresses the challenge of dynamically optimizing incentive magnitudes in advertising systems where user behavior exhibits delayed, long-range dependencies (e.g., fatigue) and global constraints must be enforced despite high-frequency interactions and non-Markovian dynamics.

id: budgeted multi-objective LLM config regret
name: budgeted multi-objective LLM config regret
description: The paper addresses the problem of optimizing noisy, vector-valued LLM configuration outcomes under strict per-configuration cost constraints and limited evaluation budgets, where traditional single-objective regret bounds fail to account for Pareto efficiency gaps and cost heterogeneity.

id: multi-objective lexicographic regret in low-rank matrix bandits
name: multi-objective lexicographic regret in low-rank matrix bandits
description: The paper addresses the challenge of efficiently learning and optimizing multiple prioritized objectives in online matrix bandits where each objective follows a low-rank structure, while existing methods either ignore the lexicographic ordering or suffer from high computational complexity in updating estimators across rounds.

id: finite-budget instability in CVaR RaQL
name: finite-budget instability in CVaR RaQL
description: The paper addresses the fragility of fixed hyperparameters in Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) risk-aware Q-learning under limited sample budgets, causing unstable value estimates, inefficient sample reuse, and persistent Bellman residual errors in financial decision-making tasks.

id: logarithmic convergence bottleneck in multiplayer general-sum games
name: logarithmic convergence bottleneck in multiplayer general-sum games
description: The abstract addresses the persistent **O(log T) lower bound on swap regret** for uncoupled learning dynamics in multiplayer general-sum games under full-information feedback, where no prior sublogarithmic individual guarantees exist.

id: scalable state-representation bottleneck in FJSP
name: scalable state-representation bottleneck in FJSP
description: The abstract addresses the **prohibitive computational cost and parameter inefficiency** of attention-based DRL models for flexible job shop scheduling (FJSP) as problem size grows, particularly their inability to parallelize sequential liquid-state dynamics for real-time inference.

id: segment-level preference feedback in PbRL
name: segment-level preference feedback in PbRL
description: The inability of existing preference-based reinforcement learning methods to efficiently leverage short, segment-wise human feedback for general stochastic MDPs, particularly in long-horizon tasks.

id: analytic uncertainty propagation in continuous control
name: analytic uncertainty propagation in continuous control
description: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately propagating predictive uncertainty (mean *and* covariance) in continuous control tasks where stochastic sampling introduces high variance and point estimates ignore covariance, breaking principled model-based reinforcement learning under uncertain observations.

id: limited-policy regret minimization in UMDPs
name: limited-policy regret minimization in UMDPs
description: The challenge of selecting and preparing a small, fixed set of policies for uncertain Markov decision processes (UMDPs) to minimize worst-case regret when only one can be deployed per execution, given operational constraints on policy count.

id: distributed regret bounds for LTI control under adversarial disturbances
name: distributed regret bounds for LTI control under adversarial disturbances
description: The paper addresses the challenge of guaranteeing sublinear regret bounds in distributed online control of linear time-invariant systems when agents must compete with centralized benchmarks using only local observations and neighbor communication, under adversarial disturbances and time-varying costs.

id: non-myopic active feature acquisition
name: non-myopic active feature acquisition
description: The problem of failing to account for future feature dependencies in greedy active learning when selecting which unobserved features to measure next under a fixed budget, limiting accuracy in sequential decision-making scenarios.

id: gradient variance in noisy input optimization
name: gradient variance in noisy input optimization
description: The problem is that standard evolutionary strategies for optimization under noisy input discard observable realized-input data, causing inefficient gradient estimation and slow convergence in applications like manufacturing tolerances, RL, and Mixture of Experts.

id: finite-horizon budget pacing in MARL
name: finite-horizon budget pacing in MARL
description: The challenge of enforcing hard energy and handover constraints *per time slot* in multi-agent reinforcement learning for wireless resource management, where cumulative budget violations cannot be detected or penalized until the horizon ends.

id: arbitrary-prior competitive analysis gaps
name: arbitrary-prior competitive analysis gaps
description: The abstract addresses the lack of universally applicable upper bounds in competitive analysis for online algorithms when arrival sequences follow arbitrary correlated priors, specifically bridging worst-case guarantees to Bayesian online design via posterior matching.

id: multi-armed bandit dominance under realized rewards
name: multi-armed bandit dominance under realized rewards
description: The challenge of accurately identifying the arm with the highest *realized* (not just expected) reward in stochastic multi-armed bandits when mean-based or pairwise methods fail to account for reward variability.

id: scalable high-dimensional feature interaction modeling
name: scalable high-dimensional feature interaction modeling
description: the inability of sequential subset search methods to handle very-high-dimensional datasets (>5k features) due to prohibitive computational cost of exhaustive candidate evaluation, limiting their ability to capture synergistic feature dependencies.

id: catastrophic forgetting in LoRA-finetuned LLMs
name: catastrophic forgetting in LoRA-finetuned LLMs
description: The paper addresses how fine-tuning large language models with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) erases original task capabilities (e.g., code generation) without requiring prior-task data or Fisher matrices, and proposes a lightweight penalty (Omega-S) to mitigate this retention loss.

id: misattributed cache-relay benefits in multi-agent LLMs
name: misattributed cache-relay benefits in multi-agent LLMs
description: The abstract identifies the problem of incorrectly crediting performance gains in multi-agent LLM systems to *specific* example-matched key-value cache relays, when the actual causal contribution of relayed caches (or their mismatched/deranged variants) remains unvalidated across diverse systems and tasks.

id: weak surface-structure record segmentation
name: weak surface-structure record segmentation
description: The paper addresses the problem of accurately reconstructing original record boundaries in flattened text—where topic-aligned records are concatenated without separators—when traditional boundary detection methods (e.g., embeddings) fail due to the absence of explicit structural cues.

id: sparse-attention content-influence misalignment
name: sparse-attention content-influence misalignment
description: The paper examines how discarding attention blocks in long-context models *systematically distorts* the relative impact of input content on outputs, breaking causal relationships between specific tokens and predictions.

id: norm-sensitive failure in gradient-free weight perturbation
name: norm-sensitive failure in gradient-free weight perturbation
description: The abstract identifies that gradient-free adaptation of language models fails predictably when perturbation *norm* deviates beyond a narrow, model-specific range—regardless of subspace dimension or basis choice—limiting its reliable applicability across scales and architectures.

id: lack of principled uncertainty calibration in safety-critical deep learning
name: lack of principled uncertainty calibration in safety-critical deep learning
description: Deep neural networks in high-stakes domains fail to provide reliable, interpretable confidence estimates for predictions, leaving critical decisions vulnerable to overconfidence in wrong predictions or underutilized uncertainty.

id: ABI generalization failure in DDM shard-dependent designs
name: ABI generalization failure in DDM shard-dependent designs
description: Neural-network-based amortized Bayesian inference for the drift diffusion model (DDM) fails to generalize across study designs because its learned parameters are tied to specific pairwise data shard structures, breaking scalability and adaptability.

id: hardware-constrained photonic BNN variational representability
name: hardware-constrained photonic BNN variational representability
description: The inability of photonic Bayesian neural networks to implement arbitrary variational families due to analog hardware limits on quantization, programming error, dynamic range, and mean/variance bounds, restricting scalable uncertainty-aware inference under real-world constraints.

id: high-dimensional token-space EBM sampling instability
name: high-dimensional token-space EBM sampling instability
description: Energy-based anomaly detection in high-dimensional token spaces (e.g., DINOv2 embeddings) suffers from unstable MCMC sampling due to geometric anisotropy and cross-dimensional correlations, preventing reliable density estimation and anomaly scoring.

id: privileged-info-induced reasoning degradation
name: privileged-info-induced reasoning degradation
description: Self-distillation with privileged information (e.g., reference solutions) fails to improve task accuracy in complex settings (QA, math, coding, multi-turn reasoning) because the teacher’s biased per-token targets misalign with correctness, penalizing exploratory reasoning tokens instead of answer-deterministic ones.

id: unreliable teacher-guided trajectory continuation
name: unreliable teacher-guided trajectory continuation
description: In on-policy distillation, standard reverse-KL training fails to distinguish whether teacher uncertainty stems from a few plausible next steps or a broad tail of low-probability candidates, and does not account for whether the student already captures those candidates well, leading to misaligned or suboptimal student trajectory generation.

id: counterfactual recoverability in trajectory supervision
name: counterfactual recoverability in trajectory supervision
description: The abstract addresses the problem of **incorrectly suppressing recoverable errors in on-policy distillation** where divergence metrics alone cannot distinguish whether a student’s erroneous trajectory prefix can still be corrected by the teacher’s guidance, leading to suboptimal selective supervision in trajectory-based learning.

id: open-ended generation with soft rubric supervision
name: open-ended generation with soft rubric supervision
description: the challenge of providing flexible, preference-based guidance (via rubrics) instead of rigid reference completions to enable diverse yet high-quality open-ended responses in domains like health and science.

id: LLM-RL instruction-induced exploration coverage gap
name: LLM-RL instruction-induced exploration coverage gap
description: The inability of instruction-conditioned RL training to systematically expand the behavioral diversity of pre-trained LLMs for mathematical reasoning tasks, where fixed instruction sets fail to improve performance in larger models.

id: long-term trajectory misalignment in multi-turn OPD
name: long-term trajectory misalignment in multi-turn OPD
description: In on-policy distillation for multi-turn agentic tasks, student deviations from the teacher’s trajectory accumulate over time, causing the teacher’s guidance to lose relevance for future states, even when initial state-level disagreement is high.

id: failed trajectory critique signal loss
name: failed trajectory critique signal loss
description: The absence of meaningful feedback from failed trajectories in search-augmented reinforcement learning (RL) for language model (LM) agents, where only binary exact-match rewards are used, discards actionable insights into failure causes.

id: reinforcement fine-tuning plateau in skill-specific problem generalization
name: reinforcement fine-tuning plateau in skill-specific problem generalization
description: The paper addresses the persistent performance ceiling in reinforcement fine-tuning for competition mathematics when synthetic data augmentation alone fails to overcome skill-specific generalization limits, even with increased data.

id: reward-distribution misalignment in heterogeneous HPC RL fine-tuning
name: reward-distribution misalignment in heterogeneous HPC RL fine-tuning
description: the inability of uniform-weight RL methods to effectively optimize LLMs across HPC tasks with vastly differing reward distributions (e.g., binary classification vs. long-form generation) due to unaccounted heterogeneity in task-specific answer lengths, accuracy ranges, and reward scales

id: noisy VLM reward brittleness in text-conditioned RL
name: noisy VLM reward brittleness in text-conditioned RL
description: The abstract targets the instability and unreliable reward signals produced by VLMs in reinforcement learning when used directly as reward models, where structural brittleness—rather than semantic errors—causes poor policy convergence and misalignment.

id: multi-stage SFT task interference
name: multi-stage SFT task interference
description: In large language models, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) under multi-stage training fails due to severe task conflicts at the parameter level, where gradient interference scales with absolute magnitude and disrupts joint task learning.

id: misaligned exploration-memory coupling in sparse-reward RL
name: misaligned exploration-memory coupling in sparse-reward RL
description: The abstract targets the failure of standard exploration bonuses and memory architectures to jointly optimize when reward signals are sparse and observation streams vary in how they require latent memory retention, leading to unmeasured interaction bottlenecks between exploration and memory in partially observable reinforcement learning.

id: multiplicity-induced structure-level credit skew
name: multiplicity-induced structure-level credit skew
description: In reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), repeated correct solution forms dominate credit accumulation due to sampling frequency, leaving rare solution structures under-rewarded in problem-solving tasks like competition mathematics.

id: sparse-reward capability underperformance
name: sparse-reward capability underperformance
description: In multi-reward RL tasks, sparse binary rewards fail to effectively drive optimization when paired with dense fine-grained rewards, causing their corresponding learned capabilities to degrade or remain unrefined.

id: federated reward model initialization bias under preference imbalance
name: federated reward model initialization bias under preference imbalance
description: The problem is that federated reward modeling fails to learn a universally adaptable shared initialization when user preference groups are imbalanced, causing minority clients to remain poorly aligned after local fine-tuning.

id: long-horizon state-returning drift in video world models
name: long-horizon state-returning drift in video world models
description: The inability to reliably verify or correct compounded state deviations in long-term action sequences due to the absence of ground-truth future states in interactive video world models.

id: scalable, supervision-free agent task generation
name: scalable, supervision-free agent task generation
description: The paper addresses the limitation of LLM agents requiring externally defined tasks or supervision signals, creating a bottleneck for scalable, diverse training by enabling task objectives to emerge directly from environment state exploration without human intervention.

id: catastrophic forgetting in non-stationary RL
name: catastrophic forgetting in non-stationary RL
description: The paper addresses how model-based reinforcement learning fails to retain prior task knowledge when environments shift, causing performance collapse in spatial navigation tasks under non-stationary conditions.

id: LLM-RL subgoal misalignment in long-horizon tasks
name: LLM-RL subgoal misalignment in long-horizon tasks
description: The abstract targets the failure of LLM-based agents to effectively translate high-level abstract plans into precise, environment-optimized actions for sequential decision-making over extended horizons.

id: bimanual policy coordination failures in WAM-guided tasks
name: bimanual policy coordination failures in WAM-guided tasks
description: The paper addresses the problem of **inaccurate or unsafe action selection in bimanual robotic systems** when World Action Models (WAMs) predict plausible futures but lack mechanisms to enforce real-time synchronization, role compatibility, and collision avoidance between arms.

id: trajectory-indexed utility dispersion in LLM agent memory
name: trajectory-indexed utility dispersion in LLM agent memory
description: The abstract addresses how growing interaction histories fragment limited feedback across an unbounded state space, causing irrelevant experiences to receive misleading rewards and enter a memory-reward trap in self-evolving LLM agents.

id: efficient full-parameter LLM post-training under GPU-hour constraints
name: efficient full-parameter LLM post-training under GPU-hour constraints
description: The paper targets the impractical training time of evolution strategies for full-parameter LLM post-training when only a few GPUs are available, addressing the bottleneck of high GPU-hour requirements in resource-constrained agentic LLM fine-tuning.

id: unreliable same-graph cross-task transfer evaluation
name: unreliable same-graph cross-task transfer evaluation
description: The abstract identifies the problem of inconsistent, biased, or leakage-prone experimental protocols for assessing how node classification and link prediction performance interact when sharing the same graph structure, undermining trustworthy conclusions about cross-task transfer.

id: sparse-graph spectral classification under Nishimori constraints
name: sparse-graph spectral classification under Nishimori constraints
description: The paper addresses the challenge of efficiently performing image classification on sparse graphs by embedding pre-trained features into a low-density parity-check graph structure while optimizing spectral embeddings at the Nishimori temperature to avoid frustrated cycles and ensure tractable inference via spectral methods.

id: inductive cardinality estimation for dynamic KGs
name: inductive cardinality estimation for dynamic KGs
description: The inability of existing learned cardinality estimators to generalize to entirely unseen knowledge graphs (including new relations) without retraining, hindering real-world deployment in evolving triplestores.

id: efficient multi-scale graph topology encoding
name: efficient multi-scale graph topology encoding
description: The abstract addresses the challenge of capturing hierarchical structural patterns (local motifs to global organization) in graphs for representation learning while avoiding the computational bottlenecks of traditional persistent homology methods (e.g., non-parallelizable diagram computations) and integrating topological inductive biases into scalable deep learning pipelines.

id: global-influence-aware link prediction
name: global-influence-aware link prediction
description: The abstract targets the challenge of integrating **large-scale, subgraph-level influence propagation dynamics** into link prediction for multi-relational graphs, where naive local features fail to capture global relational relevance.

id: latent-space node prediction without input reconstruction
name: latent-space node prediction without input reconstruction
description: The paper addresses the challenge of designing self-supervised node-level graph learning objectives that avoid input reconstruction or handcrafted augmentations by instead predicting masked nodes' latent representations conditioned on structural signals.

id: hypergraph node classification robustness to label noise
name: hypergraph node classification robustness to label noise
description: The paper addresses the failure of existing label-noise-robust methods to generalize effectively to hypergraph-structured node classification tasks, where noisy labels degrade performance due to the unique higher-order relational dependencies.

id: internal numerical structure in ICL
name: internal numerical structure in ICL
description: The abstract addresses the lack of understanding of how numerical sequences are *internally encoded* as graph-structured signals in LLM attention representations during in-context learning, particularly how hidden states and token connectivity vary with input complexity and context length.

id: inductive generalization failure in sheaf GNNs
name: inductive generalization failure in sheaf GNNs
description: The paper targets the lack of empirical validation for how **sheaf neural networks**—a GNN variant with edge-dependent restriction maps—perform under **inductive node classification** (unseen graphs at test time), where prior work only demonstrated transductive success.

id: domain-level unreliable news detection via network topology
name: domain-level unreliable news detection via network topology
description: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately classifying news domains as reliable or unreliable when traditional content-based methods fail due to mimicked credible journalism and AI-generated fabrications, by leveraging URL-sharing patterns in Telegram chats to exploit systematic network structure (assortative mixing) as a robust signal.

id: long-tail risk propagation in billion-scale credit graphs
name: long-tail risk propagation in billion-scale credit graphs
description: The problem of preserving critical, sparse risk diffusion chains across partitioned subgraphs in large-scale credit fraud detection systems where topological integrity is lost under load-balanced partitioning.

id: multivariate TSAD image-representation design gaps
name: multivariate TSAD image-representation design gaps
description: The abstract targets the lack of principled methods for mapping high-dimensional multivariate time series into multi-channel images, where existing approaches fail to systematically optimize channelization or validate vision backbones against time-domain baselines for anomaly detection.

id: out-of-distribution regime robustness in multiphase pipeline leak detection
name: out-of-distribution regime robustness in multiphase pipeline leak detection
description: The paper addresses the failure of leak detection models to generalize across varying flow regimes (e.g., bubble-to-slug transitions) in industrial multiphase pipelines, where existing methods are evaluated only under in-distribution conditions, masking real-world distributional shift limitations.

id: Federated MemAE attention aggregation failure
name: Federated MemAE attention aggregation failure
description: The inability of existing federated learning aggregation methods to effectively combine attention-based Memory Augmented Autoencoders (MemAE) in non-IID, unbalanced, edge-node-heavy environments degrades unsupervised anomaly detection performance.

id: long-horizon non-stationary traffic forecasting
name: long-horizon non-stationary traffic forecasting
description: The paper addresses the failure of recurrent models to accurately predict traffic patterns in edge computing under evolving, non-stationary conditions with long-range temporal dependencies and spatial correlations across service regions.

id: sparse-anomaly retention in energy time-series
name: sparse-anomaly retention in energy time-series
description: The inability of synthetic energy data generators to accurately preserve rare, localized anomalous events (e.g., extreme weather, infrastructure failures) due to their sparsity, temporal/geographical heterogeneity, and complex interdependencies across spatial and attribute dimensions.

id: human-interpretable novelty labeling in OWL pipelines
name: human-interpretable novelty labeling in OWL pipelines
description: The lack of actionable explanations, confidence-justified critiques, and human-readable names for novel anomaly clusters in open-world learning pipelines for oil well sensor data.

id: path-level wireless propagation representation gap
name: path-level wireless propagation representation gap
description: Existing wireless foundation models fail to capture multipath propagation dynamics in wireless signals, limiting their generalization across diverse environments and tasks.

id: CSI-based railway intruder detection and collision timing estimation
name: CSI-based railway intruder detection and collision timing estimation
description: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately detecting and localizing intruders (e.g., wildlife) in railway danger zones using synthetic Channel State Information (CSI) data, while simultaneously predicting their real-time position, velocity, and time-to-collision with trains.

id: dynamic topology resilience in LEO federated learning
name: dynamic topology resilience in LEO federated learning
description: The paper addresses the challenge of maintaining stable federated learning across LEO satellites where frequent link disruptions, short contact windows, and time-varying connectivity break centralized or synchronized training, requiring decentralized, topology-aware model aggregation.

id: scalable multi-AP coordination in dense Wi-Fi 8+ deployments
name: scalable multi-AP coordination in dense Wi-Fi 8+ deployments
description: The abstract targets the **lack of network-wide, low-overhead coordination** in beyond Wi-Fi 8 systems, where existing multi-AP coordination (MAPC) methods fail to handle dense deployments due to signaling overhead, slow convergence, and combinatorial complexity in joint transmission scheduling and rate control.

id: efficient target-discriminative feedback compression in OFDM-ISAC
name: efficient target-discriminative feedback compression in OFDM-ISAC
description: The abstract addresses the challenge of transmitting high-dimensional, clutter-sensitive sensing data (e.g., DDAE tensors) over resource-constrained SE-SF interfaces in distributed OFDM-ISAC networks without losing target-discriminative information.

id: static-neural-receiver generalization failure
name: static-neural-receiver generalization failure
description: Neural receivers trained for fixed channel conditions fail to adaptively generalize across diverse real-world wireless communication scenarios in NextG systems.

id: FTN BPSK detection under AWGN
name: FTN BPSK detection under AWGN
description: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately detecting BPSK signals in Faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) communication under additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) with limited computational resources, where classical sequence detectors like BCJR fail due to exponential complexity growth with channel memory.

id: real-time underwater vessel threat detection
name: real-time underwater vessel threat detection
description: The inability to reliably detect and localize vessels near buried submarine cables in real-world acoustic conditions using distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) data.

id: spatiotemporal atmospheric trajectory consistency in sparse-observation DA
name: spatiotemporal atmospheric trajectory consistency in sparse-observation DA
description: The paper addresses the challenge of maintaining physically plausible, temporally coherent atmospheric state trajectories when assimilating sparse real-world observations (e.g., radiosonde/surface data) into numerical forecasts, where prior methods fail to propagate information across unobserved time steps.

id: geospatial foundation model regression generalization gap
name: geospatial foundation model regression generalization gap
description: the inability of frozen geospatial foundation models to match supervised state-of-the-art performance on global-scale above-ground biomass regression tasks despite their promise for classification/segmentation tasks.

id: rule-based event misclassification in SAR time series
name: rule-based event misclassification in SAR time series
description: The abstract addresses the problem of inaccurate or inefficient single-event labeling in dense Sentinel-1 SAR time series for offshore wind infrastructure deployment phases, where traditional rule-based methods fail to achieve high precision (AUC=0.7853, perfect match=0.3508) due to temporal complexity and global-scale variability.

id: proxy-target equation leakage in degraded-factor prediction
name: proxy-target equation leakage in degraded-factor prediction
description: When proxy targets are derived from known domain factors used as model inputs, high accuracy may stem from memorizing the proxy-generating equation rather than generalizing to noisy or missing factor data, undermining robustness in soil-loss prediction under degraded soil-erodibility factor *K*.

id: mesoscale variability loss in SST downscaling
name: mesoscale variability loss in SST downscaling
description: The inability of deep learning models to retain critical kilometer-scale oceanic features (mesoscale eddies) in sea surface temperature downscaling, despite achieving low reconstruction error, due to over-smoothing and poor spectral fidelity across regional domains.

id: 3D turbulence model generalization gaps
name: 3D turbulence model generalization gaps
description: The abstract highlights the failure of learned models to generalize across 3D incompressible turbulence configurations due to insufficient physical conditioning, statistical overfitting, and fidelity-accuracy tradeoffs in dynamic forecasting tasks.

id: multi-cycle, multi-scale long-term time series forecasting
name: multi-cycle, multi-scale long-term time series forecasting
description: The paper addresses the failure of existing methods to handle time series forecasting when dominant periodicities vary per window, patches lack position-aware contextual refinement, and residual dynamics span multiple temporal resolutions simultaneously.

id: limited-site PV forecast calibration under temporal misalignment
name: limited-site PV forecast calibration under temporal misalignment
description: The paper addresses how day-ahead photovoltaic forecasting fails when new sites lack sufficient historical data, due to poor timestamp alignment, calibration sensitivity in persistence/physical baselines, and single-model overfitting to non-temporal validation splits—specifically in UK charging-station contexts where forecast errors disrupt energy scheduling.

id: sequential sensor data RUL estimation
name: sequential sensor data RUL estimation
description: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately predicting remaining useful life (RUL) from noisy, multivariate sensor data streams under dynamic operational conditions (e.g., combat aircraft engines) where traditional methods fail to capture temporal degradation patterns.

id: misaligned multi-site flood plateau prediction
name: misaligned multi-site flood plateau prediction
description: The inability of existing flood forecasting models to accurately reproduce prolonged high-water plateaus across distributed coastal monitoring stations, despite capturing temporal dynamics, due to unstable cross-site signal fusion.

id: diffusion sampling forecast trust calibration
name: diffusion sampling forecast trust calibration
description: the problem of how to dynamically adjust trust in feature forecasts at skipped denoising steps to avoid cumulative error when acceleration becomes aggressive, without requiring additional denoiser evaluations

id: multi-scale precipitation core retention
name: multi-scale precipitation core retention
description: The challenge of maintaining intense precipitation cores and their spatial organization across extended lead times in radar-based short-term nowcasting for hydrometeorological early warning.

id: spurious-correlation bias in nonlinear multivariate time series causal discovery
name: spurious-correlation bias in nonlinear multivariate time series causal discovery
description: The paper targets the failure of existing causal discovery methods to distinguish true latent/indirect causal links from spurious correlations in high-dimensional, nonlinear multivariate time series.

id: interventional response forecasting in multivariate CIR processes
name: interventional response forecasting in multivariate CIR processes
description: The paper addresses the inability of standard multivariate CIR models to predict system-wide causal shock responses—distinguishing true interventional effects from spurious historical co-movement—when one series is externally perturbed, a critical gap for stress-testing applications like CDS spreads.

id: EU-AI Act compliance in STLF pipelines
name: EU-AI Act compliance in STLF pipelines
description: Ensuring deterministic, reproducible, and auditable short-term load forecasting (STLF) for transmission-grid operations under strict regulatory constraints like the EU-AI Act.

id: plausible counterfactuals for oscillatory time-series
name: plausible counterfactuals for oscillatory time-series
description: Generating physically meaningful counterfactuals for time-series classifiers that preserves temporal structure and frequency-band discriminative information in oscillatory signals (e.g., vibration data) when perturbing raw features.

id: co-clustered pattern discovery in regular time series
name: co-clustered pattern discovery in regular time series
description: The inability to efficiently extract and identify recurring, cross-sensor motifs in highly regular univariate/multivariate time series datasets with periodic patterns.

id: flight-schedule-to-arrival-time misalignment in checkpoint throughput forecasting
name: flight-schedule-to-arrival-time misalignment in checkpoint throughput forecasting
description: The paper addresses the gap where traditional flight schedules (departure times) fail to directly model passenger arrival patterns at security checkpoints, causing inaccurate demand forecasts for staffing and operational planning.

id: decomposing revenue changes into driver attribution
name: decomposing revenue changes into driver attribution
description: The paper addresses the challenge of distinguishing between acquisition growth, repeat purchasing, and spending-per-order shifts in revenue forecasts when only aggregate sales data is available, requiring precise attribution of change drivers for accurate financial planning.

id: post-hoc tabular model drift adaptation
name: post-hoc tabular model drift adaptation
description: The challenge of adapting pre-trained tabular models to unseen concept drift without full retraining or bespoke architecture modifications, especially under real-time constraints where labeled data is sparse or inference-time limits exist.

id: sample-specific missingness in multivariate time series
name: sample-specific missingness in multivariate time series
description: The inability of existing methods to reliably adapt global inter-variable dependencies to per-sample variations and temporal non-stationarity when observations are incomplete, leading to unstable local refinement and erroneous information propagation.

id: predicting sparse, bursty HPC hardware errors
name: predicting sparse, bursty HPC hardware errors
description: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately forecasting irregular, burst-prone hardware failures in large-scale HPC systems where traditional time-series forecasting methods fail due to unstable error dynamics.

id: scarcity-constrained multimodal embedding alignment
name: scarcity-constrained multimodal embedding alignment
description: The paper addresses the challenge of aligning embeddings from pretrained unimodal encoders when cross-modal paired training data is extremely limited, requiring a method that preserves fine-grained inter- and intra-modal relationships without direct supervision.

id: scalable Grassmannian kernel approximation
name: scalable Grassmannian kernel approximation
description: The abstract addresses the computational infeasibility of classical Grassmannian kernels (e.g., projection/Binet-Cauchy) for large high-dimensional subspace datasets due to full Gram matrix requirements, proposing random feature maps with bounded rank-one projections to enable scalable, rotation-invariant kernel approximation.

id: kernel explosion/annihilation in SVM feature spaces
name: kernel explosion/annihilation in SVM feature spaces
description: The abstract addresses the instability in SVM kernel-based feature mappings where unbounded kernels risk numerical explosion or vanishing gradients, particularly in high-dimensional implicit spaces, without requiring ad-hoc scaling.

id: temporal Fisher information approximation in GFlowNets
name: temporal Fisher information approximation in GFlowNets
description: The abstract addresses the challenge of efficiently computing or approximating the Fisher information for trajectory samplers in GFlowNets when exact per-step conditional second moments are intractable, particularly in high-dimensional or temporally dependent settings.

id: inconsistent static ridge convergence
name: inconsistent static ridge convergence
description: The classical density ridge definition (static ridge) fails to account for eigenspace rotation during Subspace Constrained Mean Shift’s continuous flow, causing theoretical misalignment with the algorithm’s actual trajectory target.

id: optimal per-task training-time allocation
name: optimal per-task training-time allocation
description: Determining how to dynamically adjust training duration per task in a sequence of smoothly varying, overparameterized linear regression problems to maximize cumulative learning progress as task granularity increases.

id: manifold-aware latent diffusion in sparse data
name: manifold-aware latent diffusion in sparse data
description: The abstract targets the failure of latent diffusion models to preserve unknown Riemannian manifold geometry in low-data regimes, where Euclidean latent spaces distort intrinsic data structure.

id: finite-time ReLU neuron deactivation in modular addition
name: finite-time ReLU neuron deactivation in modular addition
description: The paper demonstrates that a single ReLU neuron trained on modular addition can lose all activity (freeze) in finite time, violating single-frequency Fourier alignment under Gaussian initialization and gradient-based optimization.

id: high-dimensional nonlinear SSM computational bottleneck
name: high-dimensional nonlinear SSM computational bottleneck
description: The abstract addresses the **excessive computational cost of spectral submanifold (SSM) reduction** for **high-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems**, where existing methods fail to scale efficiently while preserving nonlinear dynamics.

id: NIROM model-form uncertainty quantification
name: NIROM model-form uncertainty quantification
description: The abstract addresses the problem of **unreliable uncertainty estimation in parametric non-intrusive reduced-order models (NIROMs) when extrapolating or under limited data**, where traditional methods fail to capture model-form errors (e.g., basis-truncation bias) beyond Gaussian predictive variance.

id: gradient-free optimization for integral-loss functions
name: gradient-free optimization for integral-loss functions
description: The paper addresses the challenge of optimizing loss functions where gradients are intractable due to parameter-dependent integral structures, common in generative modeling, fine-tuning, and latent-variable learning.

id: simplex-constrained optimization convergence gaps
name: simplex-constrained optimization convergence gaps
description: The failure of second-order optimality conditions on product simplex spaces to align with weak second-order KKT points, hindering efficient gradient-based methods for discrete multivariate probability distributions and SRVF-based functional data registration.

id: kinetic arrest in grokking memorization
name: kinetic arrest in grokking memorization
description: the inability of standard optimization to escape a glassy, history-dependent memorization state during grokking, preventing the model from achieving slow relaxation toward generalization

id: discovering Lie-point symmetries in SDEs
name: discovering Lie-point symmetries in SDEs
description: The paper addresses the problem of automatically identifying unknown continuous Lie-point symmetries in stochastic differential equations (SDEs) from raw spatiotemporal trajectory data, without prior symmetry assumptions or templates.

id: limited Hessian surrogate generality in Newton-type optimization
name: limited Hessian surrogate generality in Newton-type optimization
description: The abstract addresses the problem that existing quadratic gradient methods (e.g., QG, SQG, QQG) are constrained to specific Hessian approximations (constant, diagonal, or BFGS-based), failing to leverage broader positive-definite curvature matrices for unified curvature-aware optimization.

id: finite-probe TV bounds for drifting finite-basis densities
name: finite-probe TV bounds for drifting finite-basis densities
description: The paper addresses how to derive **tight total-variation (TV) confidence bounds** for drifting probability distributions when only **noisy, finite-probe vector field measurements** are available in a **predeclared finite density basis**, accounting for held-out noise, operator estimation error, and residual approximation gaps.

id: audit pipeline reliability gaps
name: audit pipeline reliability gaps
description: The lack of systematic stress-testing in clinical risk model audit pipelines exposes critical failures in subgroup fairness detection, including unreliable significance thresholds, ineffective mitigation methods, undetected mechanism misdiagnoses, and non-transferable drift monitoring across patient cohorts.

id: adaptive ECG conformal prediction timing attacks
name: adaptive ECG conformal prediction timing attacks
description: The paper targets the vulnerability of adaptive conformal prediction in ECG monitoring where event reordering—without altering waveforms, labels, or scores—can suppress clinically critical ventricular class detections by exploiting delayed feedback dependencies.

id: diagnosis-code feature sparsity in EHR OUD prediction
name: diagnosis-code feature sparsity in EHR OUD prediction
description: The abstract targets the challenge of selecting sparse, clinically meaningful diagnosis codes from high-dimensional, noisy EHR data to improve predictive accuracy and interpretability for opioid use disorder (OUD) while avoiding overfitting and computational inefficiency.

id: cross-site clinical prediction transportability
name: cross-site clinical prediction transportability
description: The paper addresses the failure of clinical prediction models to generalize effectively across heterogeneous health systems due to data silos, where cross-site performance drops sharply despite centralized training gains being minimal.

id: PPG-BGL model generalization overestimation via data leakage
name: PPG-BGL model generalization overestimation via data leakage
description: The abstract highlights that **random train-test splits in PPG-based blood glucose estimation artificially inflate model performance** by ignoring participant-level leakage, masking true generalization failure (near-zero R² under stricter splits) while clinical error-grid metrics obscure this flaw.

id: model-update privacy leakage in federated EEG analysis
name: model-update privacy leakage in federated EEG analysis
description: The paper addresses the vulnerability of federated learning for clinical EEG data where individual model updates—even when raw data is not shared—can still expose sensitive patient-specific information to aggregation servers.

id: server-controlled PFL over-personalization in IoT OOD attack detection
name: server-controlled PFL over-personalization in IoT OOD attack detection
description: The paper addresses how unchecked client-side personalization in federated learning for IoT intrusion detection causes degraded generalization to unseen attack patterns, particularly under heterogeneous data distributions.

id: multi-objective federated learning with non-IID, heterogeneous objectives, and private features
name: multi-objective federated learning with non-IID, heterogeneous objectives, and private features
description: The paper addresses the challenge of training federated models in healthcare where hospitals have conflicting clinical objectives, institution-specific private features, and non-IID data distributions, while existing methods fail to handle both multi-objective optimization and client-level personalization simultaneously.

id: population-aware feature set optimization
name: population-aware feature set optimization
description: The challenge of selecting a single, deployable feature set that balances predictive performance across heterogeneous populations while protecting underperforming subgroups in tabular and public-health prediction tasks.

id: healthcare AI robustness-explainability gap
name: healthcare AI robustness-explainability gap
description: The lack of specialized frameworks for systematically evaluating and ensuring robustness and explainability in AI systems for high-stakes digital health applications (e.g., intensive care, neonatal, metabolic diagnostics) under data scarcity and distributional shifts.

id: domain-specific noise in OSFL feature fusion
name: domain-specific noise in OSFL feature fusion
description: In one-shot federated learning with domain heterogeneity, indiscriminate fusion of cross-client feature extractors introduces incompatible domain-specific noise when clients lack compatible feature distributions.

id: robust multilevel preconditioning for indefinite/nonsymmetric sparse systems
name: robust multilevel preconditioning for indefinite/nonsymmetric sparse systems
description: The paper addresses the failure of classical algebraic multigrid (AMG) heuristics—originally designed for symmetric/elliptic PDEs—to reliably precondition indefinite or nonsymmetric sparse linear systems, where their convergence guarantees degrade, leaving a critical gap in scalable iterative solvers for general scientific computing applications.

id: optimizer bias in low-rank matrix recovery
name: optimizer bias in low-rank matrix recovery
description: Coordinate-wise optimizers like Adam fail to exploit gauge symmetry in factored matrix models, causing inconsistent low-rank solution recovery across equivalent initializations in tasks like matrix sensing and transformer attention.

id: curvature-anisotropy sensitivity in momentum-based optimizers
name: curvature-anisotropy sensitivity in momentum-based optimizers
description: The abstract addresses how momentum-based optimizers like Muon fail to robustly handle loss-landscape curvature variations (anisotropy) in large-scale language model pretraining, despite mitigating gradient anisotropy.

id: MUON optimizer non-convergence in stochastic optimization
name: MUON optimizer non-convergence in stochastic optimization
description: The paper identifies and analyzes why the MUON optimizer fails to converge to the optimal solution for stochastic optimization problems (SOPs) as gradient steps increase, even for arbitrary mini-batch sizes, and provides error bounds for its generalized variants.

id: independent bias optimization in spectral weight updates
name: independent bias optimization in spectral weight updates
description: The paper addresses the limitation that treating biases separately from weight updates in spectral optimization (e.g., Muon) prevents joint spectral shaping, leading to suboptimal gradient allocation and boundary-function dynamics in affine layers during training.

id: high-dimensional PDE solution refinement
name: high-dimensional PDE solution refinement
description: The inability of coarse-to-fine mesh refinement to achieve sufficient accuracy in high-dimensional option pricing PDEs (e.g., Black-Scholes in 1–3D or Heston’s 2D spot-variance space) due to prohibitive computational cost and limited generalization across parameter combinations.

id: phase-dependent optimizer mismatch in deep learning
name: phase-dependent optimizer mismatch in deep learning
description: The abstract targets the failure of static optimizer choices (e.g., AdamW, SGD-M, Lion) to adapt to the shifting optimization demands—early-phase noise resilience vs. late-phase generalization—across deep network training phases on standard benchmarks like CIFAR-100/WRN-28x10.

id: unified mathematical abstraction of statistical learning
name: unified mathematical abstraction of statistical learning
description: the lack of a cohesive category-theoretic framework to systematically unify and generalize diverse statistical learning models and algorithms for broader mathematical rigor and interdisciplinary collaboration.

id: quantifying autism’s sameness insistence via entropy
name: quantifying autism’s sameness insistence via entropy
description: The paper addresses the lack of a formal, information-theoretic explanation for why individuals with autism exhibit rigid insistence on environmental sameness, framing it as an optimization of a novel entropy-based metric to minimize surprise and uncertainty.

id: algebraic likelihood root discontinuity detection
name: algebraic likelihood root discontinuity detection
description: Determining where algebraic likelihood-equation systems exhibit solution discontinuities (nonproperness) as data varies, a critical gap in real-root classification for algebraic statistical models.

id: query complexity in high-condition-number sampling
name: query complexity in high-condition-number sampling
description: The paper addresses the inefficiency of gradient-based query costs when simulating bouncy particle samplers and Zigzag processes under strong convexity and smoothness constraints, where the condition number κ scales poorly with dimensionality *d* and target precision ε.

id: target-population goodness-of-fit under covariate shift
name: target-population goodness-of-fit under covariate shift
description: The paper addresses the challenge of reliably testing whether a model’s fitted distribution matches an unseen target population when training data is drawn from a different source distribution, especially when the density ratio between target and source has heavy tails.

id: tight sample complexity bounds for robust PAC learning under Cressie–Read divergence
name: tight sample complexity bounds for robust PAC learning under Cressie–Read divergence
description: The paper addresses the gap in theoretical guarantees for distributionally robust PAC learning when adversarial distribution shifts are constrained by Cressie–Read divergence (beyond χ²), specifically quantifying how sample complexity scales with robustness radius ρ, target accuracy ε, and VC dimension d, while closing prior upper-lower bound discrepancies.

id: sample-efficient multicalibration for hierarchical statistical properties
name: sample-efficient multicalibration for hierarchical statistical properties
description: The paper addresses the challenge of estimating sample complexity for multicalibration when requiring simultaneous calibration across *k* sequentially identifiable statistical properties (e.g., mean, variance, skewness) in finite group families, where prior work only handles pairwise (Bayes pairs) or single-property calibration.

id: SAM’s radius-dependent flatness bias
name: SAM’s radius-dependent flatness bias
