description: The abstract addresses how the fixed perturbation radius *ρ* in Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) artificially restricts its implicit flatness bias to local minima, creating an unresolved trade-off between promoting flatness and maintaining training stability.

id: finite-sample ridge bias-variance tradeoff
name: finite-sample ridge bias-variance tradeoff
description: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately characterizing the finite-sample distribution of ridge regression when the regularization parameter scales with sample size and population coefficients are locally structured, under heteroskedastic/autocorrelated data.

id: eliminating adaptive query dependence in one-bit mean estimation
name: eliminating adaptive query dependence in one-bit mean estimation
description: The paper addresses the limitation that previous optimal one-bit mean estimation protocols for bounded-mean, bounded-moment distributions require adaptive, interactive queries to achieve minimax sample complexity, and shows this interaction can be removed without sacrificing optimality.

id: non-asymptotic log-likelihood ratio bounds
name: non-asymptotic log-likelihood ratio bounds
description: The abstract addresses the lack of tight, uniform finite-sample quantile bounds for log-likelihood ratio statistics in binary logistic regression across arbitrary design vectors and target parameters, beyond asymptotic approximations.

id: high-dimensional mixing-time bounds for ULA
name: high-dimensional mixing-time bounds for ULA
description: The paper addresses the limitation of existing theoretical guarantees for the unadjusted Langevin algorithm’s convergence rate in high-dimensional log-smooth strongly log-concave distributions, where prior Wasserstein mixing-time bounds fail to scale optimally with dimension *d* and precision *ε*.

id: interval-hitting constant bounds for piecewise-Lipschitz optimization
name: interval-hitting constant bounds for piecewise-Lipschitz optimization
description: The paper addresses the lack of tight, dimension-free bounds on the worst-case interval-hitting constant in one-dimensional local root anti-concentration for online optimization of piecewise-Lipschitz functions, particularly under arbitrary coefficient laws and singular distributions.

id: unsupervised alignment in 3D atomic structure prediction
name: unsupervised alignment in 3D atomic structure prediction
description: The lack of ground-truth labels for novel crystal phases or de novo proteins prevents supervised alignment methods from generalizing in data-scarce regimes of 3D atomic system modeling.

id: physicochemically implausible model generation in SR
name: physicochemically implausible model generation in SR
description: The abstract addresses the problem of symbolic regression (SR) producing chemically invalid or unphysical rate expressions without incorporating domain-specific constraints in kinetic model discovery.

id: scientific ML pipeline fragmentation
name: scientific ML pipeline fragmentation
description: The lack of integrated, modular, and reproducible workflows for end-to-end cheminformatics and materials informatics tasks—where researchers must manually stitch together disparate stages (data curation, representation, training, screening, etc.) despite focusing on a single component.

id: Pareto-front discovery under discrete-space budget constraints
name: Pareto-front discovery under discrete-space budget constraints
description: The paper addresses the inefficiency of Bayesian optimization in large discrete design spaces for materials discovery, where traditional methods waste evaluations on low-value regions before identifying Pareto-optimal trade-offs, limiting early convergence and cumulative Pareto-front coverage.

id: historical high-fidelity data integration in MF-BO
name: historical high-fidelity data integration in MF-BO
description: The inability of standard multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization to effectively utilize pre-existing, non-loop-involved high-fidelity observations (e.g., gold-standard data from prior experiments) in real-world tasks like molecular optimization or hyperparameter tuning.

id: cross-laboratory heterogeneous data integration
name: cross-laboratory heterogeneous data integration
description: The paper addresses the challenge of combining experimentally fragmented, heterogeneous, and partially observed thermochemical plastic-upcycling data from multiple labs into a unified, physics-consistent framework for actionable design.

id: joint-band dependency loss in Raman spectral regression
name: joint-band dependency loss in Raman spectral regression
description: The abstract addresses the problem of **inability to model correlated spectral features across distant wavenumber bands** in Raman spectroscopy regression tasks, where task-agnostic pretrained models (e.g., TabPFN) fail to exploit shared latent variation when processing wide, high-dimensional spectra as subsampled views.

id: scikit-learn-incompatible chemoinformatics pipelines
name: scikit-learn-incompatible chemoinformatics pipelines
description: The lack of seamless integration between traditional molecular fingerprinting tools and scikit-learn’s standardized Python ML ecosystem prevents efficient, reproducible chemoinformatics workflows from raw SMILES to deployed models.

id: unseen-drug, unseen-cell-line perturbation response generalization
name: unseen-drug, unseen-cell-line perturbation response generalization
description: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately predicting transcriptomic responses to *unmeasured* drug-cell combinations by aggregating responses from *biologically related but profiled* compounds in *unseen cell lines*, where traditional baselines fail to generalize.

id: multi-property generative polymer design
name: multi-property generative polymer design
description: The inability of existing generative polymer design methods to simultaneously optimize and match multiple macroscopic properties (e.g., mechanical, thermal, or chemical) in a single structure.

id: false-positive recency bias in LLM backtest validation
name: false-positive recency bias in LLM backtest validation
description: The standard cutoff-based contamination check fails to distinguish genuine temporal generalization from recency-induced performance gains in LLM backtesting, inflating apparent skill on post-cutoff questions.

id: CoT trace-behavior misalignment in poisoned reasoning models
name: CoT trace-behavior misalignment in poisoned reasoning models
description: The paper identifies the problem of **backdoored reasoning models producing attacker-controlled outputs while their chain-of-thought (CoT) traces remain undetectably benign**, undermining CoT monitoring as a safety mechanism.

id: silent measurement failures in AI
name: silent measurement failures in AI
description: The inability of evaluation metrics, monitoring systems, and training diagnostics to detect critical failure modes (e.g., reward model gaming, gradient corruption, or operational failures) while producing misleadingly normal outputs across training, evaluation, and deployment stages.

gap_flag.short_label: Silent measurement failures in AI ("Evaluation Blindness")
gap_flag.falsifiability_note: the strongest-evidenced of the three, since it has empirical backing rather than only theory. It's real if the 50-incident taxonomy and the named bug hold up to independent scrutiny -- both are checkable, not just asserted.

id: low-precision attention collapse via QK spectral runaway
name: low-precision attention collapse via QK spectral runaway
description: The abrupt failure of bfloat16 transformers during training stems from a shared query-key (QK) channel spectral instability—where singular-value explosion in QK projections triggers runaway updates regardless of the specific low-precision error source.

id: noisy trace-to-workflow dependency extraction
name: noisy trace-to-workflow dependency extraction
description: the paper addresses how to accurately extract deterministic producer-consumer dependencies from LLM agent traces that contain retries, exploration noise, and ambiguous ordering in multi-tool workflows

id: longitudinal subcortical mesh prediction
name: longitudinal subcortical mesh prediction
description: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately forecasting the continuous-time geometric evolution of subcortical brain structures from sparse longitudinal scans, where prior methods fail to jointly model arbitrary causal histories and prediction horizons while maintaining valid surface reconstructions.

id: 3D geometry-aware PEFT for BBBP
name: 3D geometry-aware PEFT for BBBP
description: The inability of existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods to model molecular spatial configurations and second-order interactions in blood-brain barrier permeability prediction datasets.

id: transferable electron-density pretraining
name: transferable electron-density pretraining
description: Lack of effective self-supervised pretraining methods for electron-density fields limits cross-task molecular representation transfer in electronic-structure-related tasks.

id: cross-site scar classification under data scarcity
name: cross-site scar classification under data scarcity
description: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately classifying pathological scars (keloids vs. hypertrophic) from clinical photographs across diverse hospital sites while suffering from limited labeled data and high acquisition variability, where traditional end-to-end models fail due to data dependency and governance constraints.

id: volume-confounding in radiomic/deep imaging features
name: volume-confounding in radiomic/deep imaging features
description: The inability of radiomic and deep imaging features to distinguish between true tumor biology signals and spurious volume-dependent or artifact-driven patterns in medical imaging datasets.

id: pathology-specific synthetic data quality assessment gap
name: pathology-specific synthetic data quality assessment gap
description: The abstract targets the failure of generic image metrics (e.g., FID/IS) to reliably evaluate synthetic histopathology images for medical downstream tasks due to their reliance on non-pathology pretrained models, leaving critical quality gaps in clinical applicability.

id: motion artifact correction in 4D CBCT
name: motion artifact correction in 4D CBCT
description: the inability of conventional free-breathing 4D CBCT to accurately reconstruct static and dynamic thoracic structures due to respiratory motion and sparse-sampling artifacts, without requiring explicit respiratory signal tracking or projection binning.

id: prognostic feature loss via survival outcome binarization
name: prognostic feature loss via survival outcome binarization
description: Binarizing time-to-event survival outcomes in clinical modeling discards censored patient data, collapses temporal dynamics, and excludes prognostically relevant features that survival-aware methods recover.

id: real-time patient-specific ablation trajectory optimization
name: real-time patient-specific ablation trajectory optimization
description: The abstract addresses the challenge of efficiently optimizing **patient-specific microwave ablation (MWA) planning**—balancing ablation coverage, organ damage, and insertion path length—where traditional numerical simulations are too slow for iterative optimization in clinical workflows.

id: hallucination-prone, subtype-specific CNB report generation
name: hallucination-prone, subtype-specific CNB report generation
description: The abstract targets the problem of unreliable, non-breast-specific diagnostic hallucinations in automated core needle biopsy (CNB) report generation, where domain-adapted models must ensure subtype-accurate, risk-controlled outputs without false positives across heterogeneous tissue samples.

id: evaluating counterfactual transplant compatibility
name: evaluating counterfactual transplant compatibility
description: the lack of a clinically actionable metric to assess how changing a recipient would improve graft survival outcomes for deceased donor kidneys in paired allocation scenarios

id: skull-induced aberration propagation modeling
name: skull-induced aberration propagation modeling
description: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately modeling how acoustic energy propagates through variable skull geometries in transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) simulations, where existing methods either lack physical fidelity or fail to generalize across unseen skull anatomies.

id: low-accuracy strain estimation from standard CMR
name: low-accuracy strain estimation from standard CMR
description: The abstract targets the problem of **inaccurate myocardial strain estimation from routine cine CMR sequences**, where existing methods either rely on costly advanced imaging or human-adjusted post-processing, limiting clinical scalability and regional precision.

id: uncertainty calibration for risk-constrained deferral
name: uncertainty calibration for risk-constrained deferral
description: The paper addresses how small language models fail to provide reliable confidence estimates that enable safe, risk-controlled deferral to humans in offline, private, or cost-sensitive deployments.

id: financial sentiment classification’s failure to predict stock returns
name: financial sentiment classification’s failure to predict stock returns
description: Despite high linguistic accuracy in classifying financial sentiment, models fail to generate statistically significant return-predictive signals across multiple horizons and datasets, even when adapted via QLoRA.

id: LLM EEG multi-task workflow competence gap
name: LLM EEG multi-task workflow competence gap
description: The inability of large language models to execute end-to-end, instruction-driven EEG analysis workflows—spanning signal processing, quantitative reasoning, and scientific interpretation—across diverse clinical and research datasets.

id: PHI surrogate detectability in masked spans
name: PHI surrogate detectability in masked spans
description: The paper examines whether downstream PHI detectors can reliably identify structure-preserving surrogate tokens (e.g., 'Maria S.' for 'Anna S.') *only* on the spans originally masked by de-identification, not just on raw text.

id: unreliable automated threat triage confidence
name: unreliable automated threat triage confidence
description: The problem is that direct-label LLMs for cybersecurity alert triage produce poorly calibrated confidence scores, failing to distinguish between high-accuracy verdicts and low-accuracy ones in real Windows endpoint detection datasets.

id: benchmark ranking instability in anomaly detection
name: benchmark ranking instability in anomaly detection
description: The lack of standardized dataset selection, evaluation metrics, and hyperparameter configurations causes inconsistent and unreliable algorithm rankings across anomaly detection benchmarks.

id: fairness-audit manipulation resistance
name: fairness-audit manipulation resistance
description: The paper addresses the problem of model providers strategically manipulating fairness audit outcomes by inferring sensitive attributes and artificially balancing group allocations to pass evaluations, particularly in regulatory contexts where audits are detectable or declared.

id: stealthy eavesdropping detection in BB84 QKD
name: stealthy eavesdropping detection in BB84 QKD
description: The paper addresses the failure of fixed QBER thresholds to detect low-rate, bursty, or asymmetric eavesdropping attacks in BB84 QKD that exploit temporal QBER patterns while remaining below conventional security limits.

id: runtime Android malware evasion detection
name: runtime Android malware evasion detection
description: The challenge of identifying malicious Android apps that activate harmful behaviors only during execution, bypassing static analysis and pre-installation screening.

id: unsupervised malware family discovery
name: unsupervised malware family discovery
description: The paper addresses the challenge of clustering unlabeled binary programs into threat families without prior labels, where existing self-supervised and tabular methods have not been systematically evaluated or optimized for this cybersecurity-specific task.

id: trade-offs in real-time EVCS IDS deployment
name: trade-offs in real-time EVCS IDS deployment
description: The abstract addresses the challenge of simultaneously optimizing intrusion detection accuracy, inference speed (99th-percentile latency), and model compactness in lightweight, IoT-embedded EV charging networks under strict deployment constraints.

id: zero-shot backdoor detection in PEFT weights
name: zero-shot backdoor detection in PEFT weights
description: The paper addresses the failure of existing weight-space backdoor detectors to generalize to unseen attack types and datasets in parameter-efficient fine-tuned models, where a lightweight classifier must reliably identify malicious models without prior exposure to their attack patterns.

id: real-time patch-level author impersonation detection
name: real-time patch-level author impersonation detection
description: The inability of existing defenses to reliably detect forged maintainer commits in real-time CI/CD pipelines using minimal patch-level code diffs and messages as behavioral signals.

id: misleading provenance-based ID alerting efficacy
name: misleading provenance-based ID alerting efficacy
description: The abstract highlights how PIDS performance claims are inflated by benchmarking artifacts (e.g., lexical novelty, weak evaluation protocols) that obscure true architectural advantages, particularly in process-level forensic utility and semantic signal quality.

id: noise-induced update bias in DP-ZO
name: noise-induced update bias in DP-ZO
description: The abstract targets the problem of **privacy-preserving fine-tuning of LLMs via zeroth-order optimization (ZO) suffering from disproportionate weighting of noisy updates due to fixed-scale aggregation, degrading model utility under differential privacy constraints.

id: adaptive transcript privacy leakage
name: adaptive transcript privacy leakage
description: the cumulative exposure of protected user attributes in long-term LLM agent interactions through repeated, memory-conditioned responses, even when attributes are never explicitly stated

id: private uncertainty quantification in Bayesian bootstrap
name: private uncertainty quantification in Bayesian bootstrap
description: The abstract addresses the challenge of ensuring differential privacy in statistical reporting while simultaneously privatizing the uncertainty quantification—specifically, the posterior sampling—of Bayesian bootstrap methods applied to sensitive individual-level data (e.g., U.S. Census returns or birthweight quantiles).

id: privacy-leaking trajectory memorization
name: privacy-leaking trajectory memorization
description: The inability to prevent mobility prediction models from reconstructing or inferring sensitive, user-specific trajectory segments from training data at varying spatial-temporal granularities.

id: interpretable unit extraction fidelity gap
name: interpretable unit extraction fidelity gap
description: The abstract addresses the problem of losing accuracy (*fidelity gap*) when extracting interpretable circuit units from dense pretrained transformers via auxiliary sparse representations or retraining, while preserving the original model’s behavior without additional training data.

id: MLP redundancy in vision transformers
name: MLP redundancy in vision transformers
description: The paper addresses the problem of unnecessary computational overhead from MLP modules in vision transformer architectures, demonstrating that they can be replaced with ReLU activations under knowledge distillation while preserving accuracy and drastically reducing parameters.

id: efficient cross-scale model parameter transfer
name: efficient cross-scale model parameter transfer
description: The paper addresses how to effectively repurpose pretrained parameters from a large transformer model (e.g., 1.4B) into a smaller sibling (e.g., 410M) without losing performance, while accounting for structural mismatches in weight alignment, initialization, and budget constraints.

id: frontier LLMs underperform on expert-level executive decision-making
name: frontier LLMs underperform on expert-level executive decision-making
description: Frontier language models fail to meet professional-grade accuracy and preference on real-world, open-ended European executive tasks—where human experts achieve near-perfect solve rates and blindly outrank model outputs.

id: tournament-wide forecast consistency gaps
name: tournament-wide forecast consistency gaps
description: The paper identifies how LLMs’ individual match predictions fail to correlate with their overall tournament performance, exposing a disconnect between granular and holistic forecasting accuracy in end-to-end event prediction.

id: consensus ranking under noisy human judgments
name: consensus ranking under noisy human judgments
description: The problem of deriving reliable ordinal assessments from heterogeneous, unreliable human ratings when ground truth is unavailable or unverifiable, particularly in decision-making tasks where model scores alone lack interpretability or coverage.

id: scalable automated relevance scoring for web search
name: scalable automated relevance scoring for web search
description: The paper addresses the challenge of replacing costly human annotation with reliable, high-throughput vision-language model judgments to enable efficient relevance evaluation and reduce statistical noise (MDEs) in large-scale online search experiments.

id: domain-specific TTS performance gaps
name: domain-specific TTS performance gaps
description: The lack of standardized, multi-metric evaluation frameworks for assessing how modern TTS systems vary in perceptual quality, speaker similarity, and acoustic fidelity *across diverse speech domains* (e.g., emotional, conversational) and *low-resource languages* remains unresolved.

id: static embeddings' marginal utility in hybrid retrieval
name: static embeddings' marginal utility in hybrid retrieval
description: Determining whether static embeddings provide meaningful complementary ranking signals when already combined with lexical (BM25) and transformer-based retrievers in Dutch information retrieval tasks.

id: fixed-link-function misspecification in paired comparisons
name: fixed-link-function misspecification in paired comparisons
description: The inability of Bradley-Terry/Thurstone-Mosteller models to adapt their win-probability transformation (inverse link function) to data, causing biased strength estimates and rankings in sports match outcomes.

id: ranking instability in attribution methods
name: ranking instability in attribution methods
description: The abstract addresses the problem of unreliable feature rankings produced by attribution methods due to stochasticity, where small variations in input or method parameters lead to inconsistent top-*k* importance rankings across repeated evaluations.

id: token-level dynamic width pruning inefficiency
name: token-level dynamic width pruning inefficiency
description: The abstract targets the **loss of accuracy and practical acceleration** caused by coarse-grained, input-agnostic dynamic pruning in LLMs, where static or layer-level sparsity fails to adapt to per-token computation needs under aggressive sparsity settings.

id: real-time diffusion VLA latency on edge
name: real-time diffusion VLA latency on edge
description: The paper addresses the challenge of running diffusion-based vision-language-action (VLA) models at high control frequencies (50–200 Hz) on resource-constrained edge devices, where compute intensity and strict latency/energy constraints prevent real-time deployment.

id: multi-turn RL reward sparsity in CUDA kernel generation
name: multi-turn RL reward sparsity in CUDA kernel generation
description: The abstract addresses the problem of **severe reward sparsity and inefficient feedback loops** in multi-turn reinforcement learning for CUDA kernel generation, where binary pass/fail rewards and high compilation latencies dilute learning signals across trajectories.

id: cross-platform GPU train-infer portability gaps
name: cross-platform GPU train-infer portability gaps
description: The inability to efficiently port **floating-point-accurate** GPU training and inference workloads across heterogeneous consumer hardware (NVIDIA/AMD GPUs, Apple/Intel iGPUs/APUs) without excessive latency, binary bloat, or correctness trade-offs.

id: heterogeneous fragility in ViT PTQ
name: heterogeneous fragility in ViT PTQ
description: The abstract addresses the problem of **uneven sensitivity to quantization across Vision Transformer components**, where uniform bit-width allocation during post-training quantization fails to account for varying fragility, degrading performance under constrained bit budgets.

id: nonstationary hardware noise adaptation in quantum syndrome decoding
name: nonstationary hardware noise adaptation in quantum syndrome decoding
description: The paper addresses the failure of fixed neural decoders to generalize across strong, heterogeneous, and evolving hardware noise conditions in surface-code quantum error correction, causing degraded performance due to distribution shifts between simulation and real hardware.

id: 4-bit quantized LLM sequential knowledge forgetting
name: 4-bit quantized LLM sequential knowledge forgetting
description: The paper addresses how **sequential memory updates in 4-bit quantized LLMs for finance** cause **catastrophic forgetting of prior factual edits** due to instability under low-bit constraints, degrading real-world applicability despite efficiency gains.

id: efficient cross-model KV cache handoff
name: efficient cross-model KV cache handoff
description: The inability to directly reuse precomputed key-value (KV) caches when switching between models of the same family during inference, forcing repeated prefill computation and breaking cost-quality cascading or dynamic routing.

id: ultra-low-rank LoRA accuracy degradation
name: ultra-low-rank LoRA accuracy degradation
description: Ultra-low-rank adapters (rank ≤ 2) lose downstream task performance in multi-tenant LoRA serving systems due to insufficient capacity, despite their efficiency gains in VRAM and PCIe overhead.

id: privacy-aware federated quantization variance
name: privacy-aware federated quantization variance
description: The abstract targets the **exponential codebook-dependent mean squared error (MSE) scaling** in privacy-preserving vector quantization for distributed optimization, where existing methods (e.g., vqSGD) suffer from unfavorable $O(4^b)$ error growth with bit-width *b* in federated learning settings like CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST.

id: scaling byte-level generation without attention
name: scaling byte-level generation without attention
description: The paper addresses the challenge of achieving competitive text generation performance at small dataset scales (2–512 MB) and low parameter counts (~0.5M) without attention mechanisms or pretraining, while maintaining human-like text quality.

id: long-sequence attention frequency-bandwidth mismatch
name: long-sequence attention frequency-bandwidth mismatch
description: the inability to efficiently prune irrelevant positional information in long-sequence attention without degrading low-frequency, globally-relevant signal retention, especially in RoPE-based models

id: graph attention normalization mismatch
name: graph attention normalization mismatch
description: Graph attention fails to generalize across homophilic and heterophilic graphs due to a fixed softmax normalization that cannot adaptively balance attention distribution granularity.

id: recurrent memory alignment in sliding-window Transformers
name: recurrent memory alignment in sliding-window Transformers
description: The inability of sliding-window attention to retain long-term dependencies across token sequences while maintaining parallelizable training in Transformers, particularly in next-token prediction tasks.

id: cardinality-loss in graph aggregation
name: cardinality-loss in graph aggregation
description: The standard virtual-node pipeline in message-passing networks loses multiplicative graph structure (e.g., node counts, motif frequencies) during global state compression, breaking downstream tasks requiring exact multiplicity preservation.

id: context-length-dependent prefill latency in edge RAG
name: context-length-dependent prefill latency in edge RAG
description: The abstract targets the **quadratic prefill latency** in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on edge hardware, where context retrieval and re-ingestion scales with retrieved document length ($O(L_{context})$), making real-time interaction impractical despite SSMs’ inherent $O(1)$ token-generation efficiency.

id: hardware-noise-aware quantization precision allocation
name: hardware-noise-aware quantization precision allocation
description: The abstract targets the problem of inefficient bit-width assignment in analog compute-in-memory (CIM) quantization due to unaccounted hardware noise floors, causing wasted precision in noisy regions and suboptimal accuracy gains.

id: hierarchical window-schedule sensitivity in 1D causal attention
name: hierarchical window-schedule sensitivity in 1D causal attention
description: The paper examines how varying the hierarchical window sizes and iteration counts in a strictly local, weight-shared attention mechanism (TextNCA) systematically affects language modeling performance on WikiText-103, revealing that the staged narrow-to-wide schedule is critical for performance, not just iteration or window size alone.

id: recurrent-state associative retrieval inefficiency
name: recurrent-state associative retrieval inefficiency
description: The paper addresses the limitation that state-space models (like Mamba-2) fail to decode token-conditioned keys from their recurrent states, preventing efficient associative memory retrieval for long-context sequence modeling.

id: hybrid-attention tree-speculation state explosion
name: hybrid-attention tree-speculation state explosion
description: In hybrid-attention LLMs, existing tree-speculative decoding systems inefficiently scale verification latency and transient memory with tree/batch size due to branch-by-branch recurrent-layer traversal and full-state materialization for every proposal node.

id: high-dimensional codebook memory bottlenecks in neuro-symbolic AI
name: high-dimensional codebook memory bottlenecks in neuro-symbolic AI
description: The abstract addresses the critical issue of excessive GPU memory consumption and scalability limitations caused by high-dimensional codebooks in neuro-symbolic AI systems, specifically when executing matrix-based vector symbolic architecture (VSA) operators.

id: inference-protocol ambiguity in LLM reasoning benchmarks
name: inference-protocol ambiguity in LLM reasoning benchmarks
description: The lack of standardized, protocol-specific reporting and evaluation frameworks for diverse test-time scaling methods obscures fair comparison of LLM reasoning performance across studies.

id: propagating error in multi-hop reasoning
name: propagating error in multi-hop reasoning
description: The inability of single-pass LLMs to correct intermediate mistakes in sequential reasoning tasks (e.g., extraction, counting, ordering) due to unchecked state propagation across inference steps.

id: black-box LLM response corruption identifiability
name: black-box LLM response corruption identifiability
description: The abstract addresses the problem of determining whether corrupted or inconsistent responses from black-box language models can be reliably distinguished from valid ones under relational transformations (e.g., paraphrasing, scaling) and anchored evidence (e.g., execution verification), and quantifying the inherent difficulty of recovery when up to *k* responses are corrupted.

gap_flag.falsifiability_note: real if γ_k(D,A) proves predictive beyond the paper's own controlled test suite. Would weaken if it fails to generalize past synthetic setups to real deployed multi-agent or verification systems.

id: distributed reasoning trajectory failures in LLMs
name: distributed reasoning trajectory failures in LLMs
description: The paper addresses how LLMs exhibit *non-localized* reasoning errors—where failures arise from cumulative, task-specific deviations in the *dynamics* of visible CoT traces (e.g., premature verification collapse or incorrect SAT assumption shifts) rather than isolated semantic errors in individual steps.

id: LLM interface refinement gap
name: LLM interface refinement gap
description: The inability of large language models to fully compensate for missing cognitive distinctions through scaling alone, requiring explicit interface refinement to achieve human-like reasoning performance.

id: self-inspection methods fail at scaling
name: self-inspection methods fail at scaling
description: Large language models’ self-critical or self-reflective generation methods (e.g., Best-of-N selection, rewriting, debate) lose accuracy advantage over naive repeated sampling as model size grows, due to diminishing returns on self-evaluation and increased token overhead.

id: Vietnamese figurative language cultural competence gap
name: Vietnamese figurative language cultural competence gap
description: The inability of existing NLP models to accurately interpret culturally specific idioms, proverbs, and pragmatic nuances in Vietnamese due to limited exposure to idiomatic complexity traits and folk knowledge.

id: decoder collapse of underrepresented cultural knowledge
name: decoder collapse of underrepresented cultural knowledge
description: Open-source LLMs fail to accurately reconstruct culturally specific mythological entities (e.g., Finnish, Slavic deities) despite retaining their representations in the residual stream, due to the decoder mapping them to dominant-tradition tokens.

id: context-dependent Ancient Greek vowel-length annotation
name: context-dependent Ancient Greek vowel-length annotation
description: The lack of a scalable, general-purpose macronizer for automatically disambiguating phonemic vowel length in Ancient Greek text based on lexeme, morphology, syntax, and genre-specific conventions.

id: demographic-bias neuron disentanglement in GLU-MLPs
name: demographic-bias neuron disentanglement in GLU-MLPs
description: The paper addresses the challenge of identifying and isolating specific neurons in GLU-MLP architectures that exhibit differential activation patterns when processing demographic attributes, without disrupting core model functionality.

id: subword-embedding initialization for LLM vocabulary extension
name: subword-embedding initialization for LLM vocabulary extension
description: The paper addresses how poorly chosen initialization of newly added subword embeddings during vocabulary extension for Hindi in a 30B-parameter LLM hinders continued pre-training efficiency, leading to suboptimal convergence and wasted computational steps.

id: LLM dimensionality collapse in tabular prediction
name: LLM dimensionality collapse in tabular prediction
description: Large language models lose predictive accuracy on tabular data as input dimensionality increases, unlike classical methods that either maintain or improve performance, due to an unexplained failure mode tied to high-dimensional input representation.

id: scalable distribution gap in shallow quantum generative models
name: scalable distribution gap in shallow quantum generative models
description: The abstract addresses the problem of whether shared classical randomness in shallow-depth quantum generative models (with bounded connectivity) can provably generate a strictly larger class of output distributions than purely unitary models at fixed depth for arbitrarily large systems.

id: QAOA-MIS shallow-circuit variance misprediction
name: QAOA-MIS shallow-circuit variance misprediction
description: The dynamical Lie algebraic (DLA) theory incorrectly predicts exponentially vanishing gradient variances for shallow QAOA circuits solving maximum independent set (MIS) on arbitrary graphs, when in reality polynomial variance growth ('cragged terrains') dominates empirically.

id: misattributed redundancy in MoE routing
name: misattributed redundancy in MoE routing
description: The abstract identifies the problem of conflating geometric subspace overlap between experts with actual functional redundancy in sparse mixture-of-experts routing, where overlapping subspaces do not equate to redundant computation for token representation.

id: phase-specific expert role degradation in MoE-VLMs
name: phase-specific expert role degradation in MoE-VLMs
description: The abstract targets the problem where global routing aggregation in MoE-VLMs obscures phase-specific expert roles (e.g., image vs. question vs. answer tokens) due to uneven token distribution, causing merged experts to lose task-relevant specialization and hurting performance.

id: Efficient Sparse Visual Tokenization for VLMs
name: Efficient Sparse Visual Tokenization for VLMs
description: Reducing computational overhead and improving efficiency in vision-language models by enabling sparse, query-relevant visual token selection or object-centric tokenization.

id: false-negative bias in negative sampling
name: false-negative bias in negative sampling
description: The abstract targets the failure of standard contrastive retrieval to downweight semantically relevant but *unmatched* documents as false negatives, degrading knowledge-based VQA retrieval accuracy.

id: VLM spatial reasoning without external priors
name: VLM spatial reasoning without external priors
description: Vision-language models fail to generalize to physically coherent spatial reasoning tasks due to reliance on external 3D priors or spatial encoders, limiting their zero-shot adaptability to embodied manipulation and spatial perception benchmarks.

id: Dynamic Visual Evidence Pruning and Allocation
name: Dynamic Visual Evidence Pruning and Allocation
description: Optimizing inference efficiency in vision-language models by adaptively selecting or allocating visual tokens to preserve performance under computational constraints.

id: Causal and Diverse Algorithmic Recourse
name: Causal and Diverse Algorithmic Recourse
description: Developing recourse methods that ensure actionable, stable, and diverse recommendations for improving high-stakes classification outcomes while mitigating strategic gaming and misalignment.

id: path-specific fairness audit fragility from causal discovery errors
name: path-specific fairness audit fragility from causal discovery errors
description: Post-hoc fairness audits fail when causal discovery omits or misrepresents the sensitive-attribute→outcome pathway critical to path-specific counterfactual fairness estimands, despite structural metrics masking these omissions.

id: Explainable and Structured Bayesian Causal Discovery
name: Explainable and Structured Bayesian Causal Discovery
description: Developing principled, interpretable, or uncertainty-aware methods for inferring DAGs from observational data with domain knowledge or statistical justification.

id: multi-step denoising reward attribution
name: multi-step denoising reward attribution
description: The abstract addresses the challenge of assigning credit for preference-based rewards across the entire noisy intermediate latents during diffusion model denoising, where sparse terminal feedback fails to guide effective gradient updates or trajectory steering.

id: recurrent ViT training robustness vs. accuracy trade-off
name: recurrent ViT training robustness vs. accuracy trade-off
description: The paper examines how recurrent Vision Transformers (bViT) balance accuracy, parameter efficiency, and robustness beyond training data under memory constraints, while clarifying the unintended architectural biases introduced by ODE-based training and deep supervision.

id: Stabilizing Robustness in DNN Training Dynamics
name: Stabilizing Robustness in DNN Training Dynamics
description: Investigating mechanisms to preserve or enhance robustness in deep neural networks during training or deployment under adversarial or hardware fault conditions.

id: real-time EEG gait state classification under motion artifacts
name: real-time EEG gait state classification under motion artifacts
description: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately classifying continuous, multi-state gait phases (Stand, Initiate, Execute, Terminate) from EEG signals in real-time exoskeleton control, despite motion artifacts and low SNR degrading traditional binary gait formulations.

id: EEG foundation model paradigm-specific adaptation bottleneck
name: EEG foundation model paradigm-specific adaptation bottleneck
description: The inability of existing EEG-based BCI foundation models to simultaneously achieve broad transferability, high decoding accuracy, and low adaptation overhead across diverse motor/neural task paradigms.

id: Collaborative and Constrained Harness Evolution
name: Collaborative and Constrained Harness Evolution
description: Improving agent harnesses through decentralized or constrained evolution to enhance generalization and performance in heterogeneous environments.

id: Dynamic Skill Evolution and Reuse in Agents
name: Dynamic Skill Evolution and Reuse in Agents
description: Investigating how agent systems can autonomously generate, refine, and reuse skills to improve performance across sequential or interconnected tasks.

id: Differentiable Feasibility in Constrained Sequential Decision-Making
name: Differentiable Feasibility in Constrained Sequential Decision-Making
description: End-to-end learning of policies that enforce hard constraints (e.g., capacity, feasibility) in stochastic sequential decision problems via differentiable optimization or dual-price mechanisms.

id: nonconcave semiparametric dynamic pricing
name: nonconcave semiparametric dynamic pricing
description: The paper addresses the challenge of optimizing revenue in dynamic pricing systems where demand follows a semiparametric surplus-index model with unknown linear valuation parameters and non-concave, non-strongly unimodal revenue functions, allowing nonunique optimal prices.

id: Q-learning TD-target overestimation under noisy Q-value uncertainty
name: Q-learning TD-target overestimation under noisy Q-value uncertainty
description: The deterministic greedy maximization in Q-learning’s TD target amplifies errors when Q-value estimates are unreliable, causing unstable overestimation in bootstrapped value updates across control tasks.

id: quantum policy approximation in finite/infinite-horizon MDPs
name: quantum policy approximation in finite/infinite-horizon MDPs
description: The paper addresses the challenge of efficiently computing approximate optimal policies in finite-horizon and infinite-horizon discounted MDPs using quantum algorithms, where classical methods struggle to meet established lower bounds on query complexity.

id: pessimistic bias in off-policy multi-step Q-learning
name: pessimistic bias in off-policy multi-step Q-learning
description: The asymmetric bias introduced by coupling suboptimal logged actions to multi-step return evaluation in off-policy reinforcement learning, which grows with horizon and distorts action-value estimates under deterministic and stochastic dynamics.

id: Offline RL Distribution Shift Correction
name: Offline RL Distribution Shift Correction
description: Addressing Q-value estimation bias and generalization errors due to distribution mismatch between behavioral and learned policies in offline RL.

id: neural critic bias-cost tradeoff in average-reward CMDPs
name: neural critic bias-cost tradeoff in average-reward CMDPs
description: The abstract targets the unresolved tension between minimizing bias and controlling optimization cost in neural critics for average-reward CMDPs, where reducing bias via NTK analysis inflates sample complexity and blocks order-optimal primal-dual convergence.

id: asynchronous Markovian sampling convergence gaps
name: asynchronous Markovian sampling convergence gaps
description: The lack of finite-time convergence guarantees for model-free discounted exponential-utility reinforcement learning algorithms under asynchronous Markovian sampling, despite their asymptotic convergence proofs.

id: utility misspecification robustness gap
name: utility misspecification robustness gap
description: The inability of existing general-utility reinforcement learning methods to handle discrepancies between the training and deployment utility functions, leading to unreliable performance when real-world utility deviates from the assumed specification.

id: layer-wise perturbation attribution mismatch
name: layer-wise perturbation attribution mismatch
description: The abstract identifies that sensitivity (representation divergence), causality (repair site for clean activations), and compensatory capacity (adapter repair location) fail to align across transformer layers for surface-perturbed language model inputs, creating inconsistent diagnostic signals for model failure analysis.

id: multiple-choice label bias in linear-attention distillation
name: multiple-choice label bias in linear-attention distillation
description: The conversion of full-attention layers to linear-attention (KDA) in large language models introduces a systematic failure where the model predicts fixed answer labels (e.g., 'A') regardless of content, despite maintaining perplexity and other metrics, due to an undetected interface injury in the training process.

id: Robust Low-Tubal-Rank Tensor Recovery from Corrupted Cross-Concentrated Sampling
name: Robust Low-Tubal-Rank Tensor Recovery from Corrupted Cross-Concentrated Sampling
description: Recovering low-tubal-rank tensors from partial cross-concentrated sampling observations in the presence of sparse, arbitrarily large outliers

id: Token-Level Credit Calibration in Self-Distillation
name: Token-Level Credit Calibration in Self-Distillation
description: Purifying and refining token-level supervision signals in self-distillation to improve stability and alignment with sequence-level objectives in RL-trained language models.

id: unreliable intermediate-decision credit assignment
name: unreliable intermediate-decision credit assignment
description: In agentic reinforcement learning for multi-turn language tasks, sparse trajectory-level rewards fail to distinguish which specific intermediate token-level decisions contribute meaningfully to success, preventing precise credit assignment for long-horizon learning.

id: RL Critic Calibration for LLM Reasoning
name: RL Critic Calibration for LLM Reasoning
description: Improving reinforcement learning critic robustness in LLMs by addressing value estimation errors and reward calibration in sparse-reward reasoning tasks.

id: behavioral locality failure in closed-loop VLA editing
name: behavioral locality failure in closed-loop VLA editing
description: Task-vector subtraction in multitask vision-language-action policies disrupts unintended controls and collapses behavior unpredictably across different skill regimes when deployed in real-world robotics tasks.

id: stale-chunk execution in VLA
name: stale-chunk execution in VLA
description: The paper addresses the problem where fixed-horizon replanning in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models forces critical manipulation stages to execute from outdated, replanned chunks when no replanning boundary intervenes.

id: Scalable Temporal Graph Community Detection
name: Scalable Temporal Graph Community Detection
description: Developing GPU-accelerated, efficient community detection methods for temporal graphs while preserving structural and temporal dynamics.

id: long-range dependency loss in large-scale GNNs
name: long-range dependency loss in large-scale GNNs
description: The problem is that graph coarsening sacrifices per-node discriminability by clustering nodes into uniform representations, while intra-cluster propagation (e.g., Cluster-GCN) breaks long-range structural information, and neither approach efficiently balances both in memory-constrained, large-scale node classification tasks.

id: long-context time-series anomaly retrieval failure
name: long-context time-series anomaly retrieval failure
description: The inability of existing time-series language models to accurately localize anomalies in long, high-frequency sequences due to degraded retrieval performance at extended contexts, particularly when evidence is sparse or buried.

id: inefficient uniform inference in sparse anomalies
name: inefficient uniform inference in sparse anomalies
description: The problem is that standard time series anomaly detection models waste computational resources by applying full inference uniformly across all data points, even though anomalies are rare and most samples are predictable normal patterns.

id: energy-constrained federated clustering for heterogeneous wireless FL
name: energy-constrained federated clustering for heterogeneous wireless FL
description: The paper addresses the problem of how to efficiently schedule and train federated learning models across wireless edge devices with stochastic energy harvesting and non-i.i.d. data distributions, where cluster-aware scheduling must balance global representativeness and personalized model adaptation under communication and energy constraints.

id: client-aware federated TSFM adaptation
name: client-aware federated TSFM adaptation
description: The challenge of balancing cross-building transfer and building-specific temporal pattern capture in federated learning for time-series foundation models when client data are non-IID and private.

id: under-representing extreme heat peak intensities
name: under-representing extreme heat peak intensities
description: Deep learning weather emulators fail to accurately capture the maximum intensity of extreme heat events in 10–15 day forecasts, despite showing skill in deterministic temperature prediction.

id: diurnal variability prediction failure in non-Earth atmospheres
name: diurnal variability prediction failure in non-Earth atmospheres
description: The abstract identifies that zero-shot Earth-trained weather models fail to capture Martian diurnal temperature and wind cycles, instead converging toward climatological means, despite accurate current-condition depiction.

id: underestimating drought lower-tail risk via reanalysis-only bounds
name: underestimating drought lower-tail risk via reanalysis-only bounds
description: The paper addresses the failure of historical reanalysis data to capture severe, low-probability drought extremes during anomalously dry periods, leading to underestimation of worst-case drought risk in regional forecasts.

id: uncertainty-aware probabilistic tsunami inundation prediction
name: uncertainty-aware probabilistic tsunami inundation prediction
description: The paper addresses the failure of current deterministic tsunami inundation models to quantify uncertainty in near-field scenarios (e.g., megathrust earthquakes), leading to overconfident safety assumptions outside true hazard zones, while existing ML approaches lack calibrated probabilistic outputs.

id: latent phase misalignment in drifting periodic time series
name: latent phase misalignment in drifting periodic time series
description: The paper targets the failure of fixed-grid time series models to handle shifting cycle phases and timing in latent representations, where phase-related variability degrades forecasting accuracy under periodicity drift.

id: directional change misalignment in low-magnitude time series
name: directional change misalignment in low-magnitude time series
description: Standard forecasting losses (e.g., MSE) fail to capture the correct *up/down* trend of small-magnitude time series shifts, a critical limitation in risk/financial forecasting where directional accuracy matters as much as magnitude.

id: latent-regime-specific volatility underprediction
name: latent-regime-specific volatility underprediction
description: The paper addresses how aggregate volatility forecast metrics (e.g., RMSE/MAE) obscure regime-dependent failures—particularly tail underprediction and conditional bias—that critically undermine risk management in cryptocurrency and ETF markets.

id: misalignment between generic forecasting metrics and domain-specific decision utility
name: misalignment between generic forecasting metrics and domain-specific decision utility
description: Existing time-series benchmarks fail to evaluate models on metrics that directly correlate with real-world financial decision-making (e.g., directional accuracy over point-wise error), leaving gaps in assessing practical forecasting utility for economic applications.

id: Time Series Feature Engineering for Classification
name: Time Series Feature Engineering for Classification
description: Optimizing feature extraction methods to improve time series classification (TSC) performance across diverse datasets.

id: finite-temperature perceptron generalization gap
name: finite-temperature perceptron generalization gap
description: The abstract addresses the challenge of quantifying and closing the gap between training loss and generalization error in a finite-temperature continuous-spin perceptron via variational bounds on the quenched pressure for Gaussian-mixture data.

id: geodesic flow constraints in quantum-classical hybrid learning
name: geodesic flow constraints in quantum-classical hybrid learning
description: The paper addresses the problem of how to model and optimize learning dynamics on product Wasserstein manifolds (classical layers + quantum parameters) as geodesic flows, where distributional constraints are reframed as intrinsic geometric structures rather than capacity-limiting restrictions.

id: Boundary Term Consistency in Reflected Diffusion
name: Boundary Term Consistency in Reflected Diffusion
description: Ensuring mathematically valid boundary conditions (no-flux, conormal trace) for reflected diffusion processes in bounded domains to guarantee Lagrangian flow regularity and score-based learning correctness.

id: Unifying diffusion process design for training and sampling
name: Unifying diffusion process design for training and sampling
description: Exploring theoretical frameworks to reconcile simulation-free training with finite-time generation in score-based diffusion models.

id: pseudorandom orbit structure leakage in diffusion
name: pseudorandom orbit structure leakage in diffusion
description: The deterministic numerical orbits from pseudorandom number generators in finite-precision diffusion models become learnable inputs that systematically distort training loss gradients and degrade generation quality, violating the assumption of independent, identically distributed randomness.

id: Theoretical Guarantees for Optimal Transport via Flow Matching
name: Theoretical Guarantees for Optimal Transport via Flow Matching
description: Establishing rigorous theoretical foundations for flow-based generative models, particularly ensuring convergence to optimal transport couplings under specific conditions.

id: non-nested sigma-algebra convergence in finite-rank function flow matching
name: non-nested sigma-algebra convergence in finite-rank function flow matching
description: The paper addresses the failure of martingale convergence guarantees in functional flow matching when finite-rank approximations (e.g., coefficients or point evaluations) under scattered or adaptive refinement produce non-nested conditioning sigma-algebras, breaking asymptotic consistency in sensor-limited settings.

id: 12-lead ECG model failure in single/multi-lead point-of-care
name: 12-lead ECG model failure in single/multi-lead point-of-care
description: Existing ECG foundation models, designed for fixed 12-lead inputs, perform poorly or break entirely when applied to real-world point-of-care devices that capture only 1–2 leads, requiring either zero-padding or architectural hacks to function.

id: inconsistent benchmarking of ECG foundation models
name: inconsistent benchmarking of ECG foundation models
description: The lack of standardized, leakage-controlled evaluation protocols prevents fair comparison of pretrained ECG models for atrial fibrillation detection across diverse datasets and deployment conditions.

id: privacy-preserving metadata clustering in CFL
name: privacy-preserving metadata clustering in CFL
description: The inability of existing metadata-based clustered federated learning methods to integrate with standard privacy-preserving mechanisms (e.g., encryption) while maintaining communication/computational efficiency in heterogeneous federated settings.

id: fairness-aware client selection bias in FL
name: fairness-aware client selection bias in FL
description: The abstract addresses how overly biased client selection—driven by imperfect datasets (non-IID, noisy, or skewed)—degrades federated learning performance, despite being used to mitigate accuracy or convergence issues.

id: output-projection optimization in Mamba-2
name: output-projection optimization in Mamba-2
description: The paper investigates why Muon’s spectral optimization benefits only the output projection—rather than input or both—when fine-tuning Mamba-2, despite its theoretical advantage for conditioning, and how this localized gain improves token efficiency beyond compute-optimal convergence.

id: MoE expert gradient temporal conditioning failure
name: MoE expert gradient temporal conditioning failure
description: The abstract identifies that stateless Sinkhorn optimizers fail to handle temporally varying, conditional gradients in routed Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) expert matrices, degrading evaluation performance in large-scale pretraining settings.

id: Occam's Razor in Modern ML Generalization
name: Occam's Razor in Modern ML Generalization
description: Theoretical justification and critique of Occam's razor as a principle governing model simplicity preferences in deep learning's generalization behavior.

id: certificate complexity vs. communication complexity separation
name: certificate complexity vs. communication complexity separation
description: The paper addresses the gap between *0-certificate complexity* (the minimal size of a proof certifying unsatisfiability) and *communication complexity* (the minimal information exchange needed to solve a distributed decision problem) for DNF formulas, specifically constructing examples where the former is quadratically larger than the latter.

id: worst-case exponential pattern-counting hardness
name: worst-case exponential pattern-counting hardness
description: The paper addresses the challenge that exact or approximate algorithms for counting (permutation) patterns in sequences require exponential time in pattern length *k* in the worst case, despite the problem’s inherent asymmetry favoring average-case efficiency.

id: partition learning with unknown part count
name: partition learning with unknown part count
description: The paper addresses the challenge of efficiently learning a hidden partition of an *n*-element universe when the number of parts *k* is unknown, improving upon deterministic algorithms' round/query tradeoffs and proving fundamental lower bounds for randomized approaches.

id: Gaussian-averaged ReLU NTK Gram invertibility
name: Gaussian-averaged ReLU NTK Gram invertibility
description: The paper addresses the worst-case lower and upper bounds on the smallest eigenvalue of ReLU Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) Gram matrices formed by averaging Gaussian-weighted gated inner products of unit vectors, revealing tight scaling with their projective separation.

id: polynomial-time hardness of sparse least-squares
name: polynomial-time hardness of sparse least-squares
description: The abstract proves that no randomized polynomial-time algorithm can achieve near-optimal sparse least-squares solutions with sparsity scaling sublinearly in the restricted condition number for rational full-rank instances.

id: SMILES-text semantic misalignment in chemistry NLP
name: SMILES-text semantic misalignment in chemistry NLP
description: The abstract addresses the problem of **loss of molecular semantics during domain-adaptive pre-training**, where models trained on SMILES representations forget foundational chemical meaning while overfitting to syntactic patterns in scientific text.

id: loss of chemical-space topology in multimodal drug discovery embeddings
name: loss of chemical-space topology in multimodal drug discovery embeddings
description: Multimodal representation learning for drug discovery fails to maintain the intrinsic geometric and structural relationships between molecules when aligning chemical and phenotypic data, degrading downstream tasks like bioactivity prediction and molecular retrieval.

id: surrogate-driven design certification failure modes
name: surrogate-driven design certification failure modes
description: the lack of provable safety criteria for replacing expensive evaluations with model predictions in iterative design tasks, where near-perfect accuracy does not guarantee trustworthy candidate selection

id: lab-specific chemical reasoning benchmarking
name: lab-specific chemical reasoning benchmarking
description: Evaluating language models on *independent* synthetic chemistry tasks (e.g., reaction prediction, catalyst selection) using *private, proprietary lab data* to avoid training leakage and assess real-world wet-lab reliability.

id: real-time LLM agent failure detection without full-step judging
name: real-time LLM agent failure detection without full-step judging
description: The paper addresses the challenge of identifying mid-execution failures in LLM agents (e.g., loops, tool errors, goal drift) using only low-cost, microsecond-level telemetry from observable step outputs—without relying on expensive per-step evaluation by a second LLM or retraining across datasets.

id: LTL-monitor coverage collapse under high-entropy attack distributions
name: LTL-monitor coverage collapse under high-entropy attack distributions
description: Fixed-invariant LTL/FSA safety monitors fail catastrophically when attack patterns are highly dispersed (high Shannon entropy), as no tractable finite invariant set can generalize across structurally diverse triggers.

id: kinetic phenotyping of ESMs
name: kinetic phenotyping of ESMs
description: The abstract addresses the problem of **discarding critical kinetic information** in functional characterization of Engineered Skeletal Muscle Tissues (ESMs) due to **high mathematical complexity of mechanistic models**, limiting scalable adoption in disease modeling and pharmacological screening.

id: single-cell expression vector distribution alignment
name: single-cell expression vector distribution alignment
description: The paper addresses the challenge of generating biologically plausible single-cell gene expression vectors that faithfully match the true statistical distribution of a given cell type, while characterizing how model scaling affects this fidelity.

id: Decoupled Label Noise Mitigation in Medical Imaging
name: Decoupled Label Noise Mitigation in Medical Imaging
description: Improving robustness of medical imaging models by addressing label noise through per-sample trust estimation and decoupled reliability assessment for observed and pseudo-labels.

id: uncertainty-aware AL strategy selection
name: uncertainty-aware AL strategy selection
description: The paper addresses the problem of **selecting an active-learning sampling strategy in medical image classification before full annotation budgets are spent**, where poor choices can inflate labeling costs due to unaccounted uncertainty in clinical performance thresholds.

id: decoder-LLM calibration sensitivity to quantization and prompt engineering
name: decoder-LLM calibration sensitivity to quantization and prompt engineering
description: The paper identifies how **precision quantization (FP16→INT8→INT4) and prompt template/scoring rule choices** unpredictably alter calibration and accuracy in biomedical LLM classifiers, with template effects (7–24% accuracy shifts) often exceeding model selection trade-offs, and quantization-induced accuracy swings (up to +4.2%) that vary by model specialization and template.

id: prompt-scoring calibration sensitivity in biomedical LLM classification
name: prompt-scoring calibration sensitivity in biomedical LLM classification
description: The reliability of decoder LLM-based biomedical sentence classifiers (e.g., PubMed RCT outcomes) is highly unstable under variations in prompt templates, verbalizer mappings, and scoring rules (summed vs. mean token log-likelihood), with calibration errors shifting dramatically (e.g., BioMistral’s ECE swinging from 0.097 to 0.289) while accuracy changes minimally, exposing a critical gap in experimental reproducibility for low-precision (INT8/INT4) deployment scenarios.

id: semantic-structure leakage in obfuscated LLM embeddings
name: semantic-structure leakage in obfuscated LLM embeddings
description: Obfuscated language model embeddings retain exploitable semantic patterns that enable high-accuracy token recovery despite perturbation, undermining the assumed security of obfuscation-based defenses.

id: Adversarial RAG Manipulation via Semantic Exploitation
name: Adversarial RAG Manipulation via Semantic Exploitation
description: Exploiting semantic vulnerabilities in RAG systems to manipulate LLM outputs through adversarial or poisoning attacks while preserving query meaning

id: cumulative privacy leakage in dynamic graph updates
name: cumulative privacy leakage in dynamic graph updates
description: The paper addresses how repeated model retraining on evolving graph data exacerbates privacy risks by accumulating edge-level exposure over time, requiring a framework that bounds total privacy loss regardless of update frequency or schedule.

id: feature-space shortcuts in encrypted predictors
name: feature-space shortcuts in encrypted predictors
description: The paper addresses the security vulnerability where offloading a public encoder to reduce encrypted computation inadvertently exposes the private predictor’s feature-to-output mapping, enabling adversaries to bypass the original model’s input-to-output security guarantees.

id: FFN Geometry in Transformer Residual Dynamics
name: FFN Geometry in Transformer Residual Dynamics
description: Understanding how feed-forward networks (FFNs) shape residual-direction space and geometric transformations in Transformer layers.

id: reference-free LLM output ranking instability
name: reference-free LLM output ranking instability
description: The abstract targets the lack of scalable, domain-agnostic methods to reliably rank LLM-generated outputs without reference standards or human effort, addressing inconsistencies in pairwise comparisons and confidence thresholds.

id: Strategic and Efficient Text Evaluation Alignment
name: Strategic and Efficient Text Evaluation Alignment
description: Ensuring evaluation metrics for LLM outputs are robust against manipulation while optimizing human evaluation effort for model ranking.

id: adaptive sparse kernel selection for GPU
name: adaptive sparse kernel selection for GPU
description: The lack of a universally optimal sparse matrix representation or execution strategy for GPU-accelerated sparse linear algebra (SpMV, SpMM, SpGEMM) across varying sparsity patterns and hardware, causing inconsistent performance gaps (e.g., 350x) between formats like CSR and Blocked-ELL on the same workload.

id: inefficient GPU spMspV for dual-sparse LLM inference
name: inefficient GPU spMspV for dual-sparse LLM inference
description: The abstract targets the sub-problem of **poor GPU kernel performance for Sparse Matrix-Sparse Vector (spMspV) workloads** in **dual-sparse LLM inference**, where existing hardware fails to exploit combined unstructured weight pruning and runtime activation sparsity efficiently for single-user decoding.

id: Hardware-Aware Sparse Attention for Long-Context Efficiency
name: Hardware-Aware Sparse Attention for Long-Context Efficiency
description: Reducing computational and memory bottlenecks in sparse attention for long-context LLMs via indexing, hashing, or hardware-algorithm co-design.

id: Attention-Aware KV Cache Quantization Optimization
name: Attention-Aware KV Cache Quantization Optimization
description: Minimizing distortion in attention products or output-aware errors during KV cache quantization for long-context LLMs.

id: token-essentiality-aware KV cache compression
name: token-essentiality-aware KV cache compression
description: The problem is that existing KV cache compression methods either permanently discard tokens (risking loss of critical context) or fail to achieve sufficient compression while retaining full precision, leaving long-context LLM inference memory-bound without a scalable, lossless solution.

id: vocabulary-logit distribution perturbation in quantized LM-heads
name: vocabulary-logit distribution perturbation in quantized LM-heads
description: Quantizing the final language-modeling head (LM-head) of large language models disrupts the vocabulary-logit distribution, degrading performance when naive compression is applied to BF16/FP16-projected outputs.

id: single-checkpoint multi-bit precision mismatch
name: single-checkpoint multi-bit precision mismatch
description: The inability of existing quantization methods to efficiently adapt a single model checkpoint to multiple bit-widths (2–8 bits) while maintaining calibration-free accuracy under diverse deployment constraints.

id: unreliable early-termination accuracy in LLMs
name: unreliable early-termination accuracy in LLMs
description: The paper identifies that truncating or prematurely stopping large language model reasoning—whether via token limits, prompts, or effort settings—does not guarantee better correctness, as early answers may be wrong or probabilistically weak, especially when compared to unfinished high-effort runs.

id: limited transparency in model correctness monitoring
name: limited transparency in model correctness monitoring
description: The problem is that LLMs’ *self-generated reasoning summaries* fail to reliably expose correctness cues when prompts are visible, leaving users with insufficient observability to judge answer validity compared to full reasoning traces.

id: open-weight models' inflectional morphology gaps
name: open-weight models' inflectional morphology gaps
description: The absence of standardized benchmarks for evaluating how well open-weight language models generalize to *productive* inflectional morphology in morphologically rich languages like Modern Greek, especially for low-frequency forms.

id: linguistic-proficiency vs. fluency gap
name: linguistic-proficiency vs. fluency gap
description: The abstract targets the failure of multilingual models to distinguish true linguistic proficiency (e.g., grammar correctness) from superficial fluency (e.g., translation smoothness) across diverse, low-resource languages.

id: inference-backend-induced benchmark variability
name: inference-backend-induced benchmark variability
description: Benchmark scores for language models are systematically distorted by unaccounted-for differences in inference frameworks (e.g., HuggingFace, vLLM), even under deterministic decoding, creating non-backend-agnostic performance metrics.

id: LLM prediction-set coverage failure under configurable inference shifts
name: LLM prediction-set coverage failure under configurable inference shifts
description: The paper addresses how arbitrary changes to inference pipelines (e.g., prompt templates, decoding temperature, quantization) break conformal prediction’s finite-sample coverage guarantees for LLMs by introducing unmodeled distribution shifts in nonconformity scores.

id: quantum measurement reconstruction via relative-entropy minimization
name: quantum measurement reconstruction via relative-entropy minimization
description: The abstract addresses the problem of how to optimally reconstruct quantum measurements from a classical-to-quantum preparation channel using a relative-entropy minimum change principle, ensuring minimal information-theoretic deviation from the forward process.

id: phase-space-invariant bosonic state fidelity estimation
name: phase-space-invariant bosonic state fidelity estimation
description: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating fidelity for bosonic quantum states that vary under phase-space translations, rotations, or other transformations—where traditional methods fail due to reliance on single-target state assumptions—using adaptive Wigner function reconstruction from limited measurements.
